correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-foc.formal: A hyperbolic (Witt) pair $e_+, e_-$ in a real Clifford algebra yields the null pair $f = \tfrac12(e_+ + e_-)$, $f^* = \tfrac12(e_+ - e_-)$ with $f^2 = f^{*2} = 0$, $ff^* + f^*f = 1$, and the ladder pairs of a Witt decomposition act on the exterior algebra of the creation span as a fermionic Fock module, irreducibly when the form is split. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[\S7]{ButlerT1}; \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT3}. The complexified version needed below is proved in Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra} rather than imported, since the maximal isotropic planes of $V_\C$ are larger than the real Witt index allows.
correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-foc.technical:
In a real Clifford algebra a hyperbolic (Witt) pair $e_+, e_-$ gives the null pair $f = \tfrac12(e_+ + e_-)$, $f^* = \tfrac12(e_+ - e_-)$, with $Q(f) = Q(f^*) = 0$ and $ff^* + f^*f = 1$: one annihilation and one creation operator for a single fermionic mode.

The ladder pairs of a Witt decomposition act on the exterior algebra of the creation span as a fermionic Fock module, and this module is irreducible when the form is split. The imported statement is the real one; the complexified version, where the maximal isotropic subspaces are larger than the real Witt index allows, is proved separately in the store rather than imported.
correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-foc.lay: Two directions in this kind of algebra, one squaring to plus one and one to minus one, can be recombined into two elements of zero length that behave exactly like the operators that create and destroy a single fermion. Several such pairs together act on a space of states built by filling or emptying each mode, the usual Fock space of fermions. This is an imported result over the real numbers; the complex version is treated separately.

__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-setting-impo: Two dimension counts we use, $\dim_\R \Cl(2,4) = 2^6 = 64$ and $\dim_\C \Cl(2,4)_\C = 64$ for the complexification $\Cl(2,4)_\C = \Cl(2,4)\otimes_\R\C \cong \Cl_6(\C)$, the second of which is checked in the verification script (the first follows from it, since complexification doubles the real dimension); Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.dimensions-real-form} records where they place the algebra in the standard tables. Two letters are reused with the tractor literature's meanings wherever a tractor is written in its scale splitting (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations-scale-tractor} and \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}, Corollary \claimref{correspondence.one-statement-three-languages}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}): inside the tractor triple $(\sigma, \mu, \rho)$, $\sigma$ and $\rho$ are the top and bottom slots, and $\rho_g$ is the bottom slot of the scale tractor; outside a triple, $\rho$ is the spinor action and $\sigma$ the pairing of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}, and $\sigma_a$ with a direction index is the soldering summand of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}. Throughout, ``twistor space'' means the module $\T$ constructed in Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}; no prior twistor formalism is assumed, and the contact with Penrose's conventions is made in the section “Incidence encodes the completion”. We fix once an orthonormal basis $a_1, a_2$ (norm $+1$), $b_1, \dots, b_4$ (norm $-1$) of $V$, with $\nO, \nInf$ in the span of $a_1, b_1$. The verification script works with $C(v) := c(v)/\sqrt2$, for which $\{C(u), C(v)\} = \ip{u}{v}$; every identity below is stated for $c$ and checked for $C$, the two differing only by powers of $\sqrt2$.
__notes__.note.correspondence.point-contact-planes: Clause (1) is the classical statement that in six ambient dimensions every chiral spinor is pure (Cartan, Chevalley \cite{Chevalley54}); the annihilator planes of spinors in the conformal spinor space $\CS$ are one ruling family of maximal isotropic subspaces, in twistor language the $\alpha$-planes of complexified compactified Minkowski space, and the $\CSm$-family are the $\beta$-planes \cite{Penrose1967, PenroseRindler86}. The transport reading adds the physical origin: the three pairs of clause (2) are ladder pairs of exactly the kind the completion produces (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}), and the tower paper \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT3} shows each further ascent adjoins one more pair, doubling the half-spinor space: the tower is a qubit register, and the conformal spinor space (twistor space) is the chirality half of its three-qubit floor. \emph{First quantisation, in this precise sense, is the Chevalley functor from ambient directions to Fock states; it is forced at the singular locus by the no-go theorem} \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1}.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} assigns the twistor restatement of its spectrum condition to this paper's setting; the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} cites the twistor reading of the completion's spinor module as a point of contact; the spectrum paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} imports the ordering shift of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}(4); the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} imports nothing from this paper: the summand decomposition of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}(1) reappears there, in the frozen point's scale, as its own Lemma 2.5(iii), proved directly; the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} imports the pure-spinor identification of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, the chart normalisation of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}, and the palatial quadratics of Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} imports the spinor identification, the pure-spinor theorem and the shared core (Theorems \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}, \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}); the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} imports the Witt-flag reading of the ladder pairs; the synthesis paper T16 \cite{ButlerT16} imports the point embedding and the Fock-vacuum reading; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.
__notes__.note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what: Every tower has rungs, the $(1,1)$ ascent adjoining a hyperbolic plane at each floor (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so at tower level every residue is flaggable (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) and flaggability selects nothing. The flag counts no towers; it orients them (the section “The arrow counted”), and it equips them: a flag on $H_{k}$ is equivalently the complex structure $J_{k}$ on the complexification $H_{k} \oplus I_4H_{k}$ (the plane $H_{k} \otimes \C$, with the field theory's imaginary unit $I_4$, which commutes with every vector of the plane) whose $-I_4$ eigenline is the annihilated half (it lives in the complexification, since no real endomorphism squaring to $-1$ has the two real null lines as eigenlines), and the ladder pair's number operator generates a $U(1)$ commuting with the rest of the rung. So every flagged tower carries rung-level abelian charges, one per rung, whatever its ground type, as this tower's derived content acquires its $U(1)$ from three ladder pairs \cite{ButlerT12}.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-mode-continuum: The boundary mode space of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} has countably many modes because the boundary modes, the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary, one per point, are aggregated over the s-wave channels into the countable array of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}. The tower of iterated completions is the algebra's model, not the source of the count: its limit is the CAR algebra with the adjoined null pairs as modes (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), while on the physical closure one ascent completes the description (Corollary \claimref{tower.answers-iteration-question}). The physical spectrum is emitted into a continuum of frequencies and a tower of angular channels, and this section carries the state theorem across that idealisation with the levels declared: what is exact, what is an inductive-limit result, and what is a modelling identification are separated.
__notes__.note.hawking.free-fermion-thermal-field-: Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-thermal-representation} is the continuum instance of T5's single-mode picture: the doubling is the completed pair structure mode by mode, the GNS vector is the thermofield double, and the modular flow is the boost. ``Free-fermion thermal field theory as the algebra carrying the mode continuum'' is now a theorem-backed description: the algebra is $\CAR(\mathfrak{h})$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra} plus Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}), the state is the I-state (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum}), and the representation it generates is the standard thermal one. \emph{Point of contact:} Israel's thermofield reading of the eternal black hole \cite{Israel1976} is exactly this representation with the second copy read as the far wedge; T5's eviction dynamics runs inside it.
__notes__.note.hawking.setting-position-series:
This paper is T7 of the series. \emph{It relies on six predecessors:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} and the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the completed-pair language and the transport principle; the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the CAR limit that makes the boundary modes an algebra (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for modular descent under its premises (P) and (R), the bosonisation bridge under (Q), and the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$ (Facts \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation} and \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}); the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the exterior exactness that greybody inheritance rests on (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-exterior-exactly-general-relativity}); and the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the ordering shift from which Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift} is promoted.

__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-frozen-point: The rung of this world is $\Cl(2,4)$, obtained from $\Cl(1,3)$ by adjoining a hyperbolic pair, one generator of each sign, whose null combinations are the zero divisors the transport resolves (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, Definition \claimref{obj.odd-extensions.single-extension}). The frozen point of the dark-energy paper is a vector in that rung, and its norm is the cosmological constant. This section shows that $I$ and the Stelle-West vector $V$ are the ascent's pair, signed by $\Lambda$, and that the odd extensions of the section “What a single generator does” are the intermediate algebras of this world's own ascent, with the degenerate case at $\Lambda = 0$ the wall of the sheaf paper.
__notes__.note.tower.why-tower: Rule 1 is the only rule that iterates: by \cite[Prop.~7.4]{ButlerT1} the fusion rule occurs at most once along any transport history and a pure Rule-1 lineage stays fusion-free, so the minimal repeated completion is exactly Definition \claimref{obj.tower.tower}. Minimality and uniqueness at each step are \cite[Thm.~4.13]{ButlerT1}, so the tower is the canonical iterated repair, not one choice among many.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.holographic-coincide: Writing, as here, $\Cl(2,4)$ for the Clifford algebra of the flat space in which $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}$ is the hyperboloid, and likewise for the other hyperboloids: the rung is the algebra of $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}$, whose isometry group $SO(2,4)$ is the conformal group of this world; the intermediate $\Cl(2,3)$ is the algebra of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ and, by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers}, the conformal ambient of the three-dimensional residue-$7$ shadow, the group theory of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}/\mathrm{CFT}_{3}$; the de Sitter intermediate $\Cl(1,4)$ is the ambient of the Euclidean three-dimensional shadow $(0,3)$, also of residue $5$, the group theory of $\mathrm{dS}/\mathrm{CFT}$. All of this is the standard fact that the isometry group of $\mathrm{AdS}_{d+1}$ is the conformal group in $d$ dimensions, which any conformal field theory in $d$ dimensions shares whether or not a bulk exists; the note adds only the residues. The coincidence does expose a difference in what two frameworks say about one pair of algebras. Holography takes the bulk and its boundary to be one physics in two descriptions. The series takes the residue of a sector to be the signature of its soldered space (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}), which a conformal class carries as well as a metric, so the boundary of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ has residue $7$ and lies, by Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, in a tower distinct from the bulk's; whether a conformal class with no chosen scale is also a superselected sector, Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue} speaking of the one metric, is a separate question and is not settled here; and the series' superselection is a statement about operators soldered to one metric, which a holographic dictionary is not. Whether that last difference means the two frameworks are speaking about different things, or that one of them is wrong about this pair, is not argued anywhere in the series and is not argued here; the remark records the question and claims nothing about the dynamical content of holography, to which the series has no counterpart.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-soldering-de: the section “The clock, and the paths between the oriented towers” placed the four extensions on the four odd towers as algebras. The dark-matter paper's definition of the residue is not algebraic, and applying it settles which tower the frozen point's algebra belongs to.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.one-operator-sees-di: An operator linear in $e_{5}$ alone, a term $\bar\psi e_{5}\psi$, is the one place the doubling would show: $e_{5}$ is the real pseudoscalar in one tower and the pseudoscalar times a central complex unit in the other, the central pseudoscalar of the complexified extension (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}; $I_5$ when the extension is $\Cl(2,3)$), which in the physicists' notation, with their complex unit read as that central pseudoscalar, is $\gamma_{5}$ against $I_5\gamma_{5}$ for $\gamma_{5} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ (with the Hermitian $\gamma_{5} = I_{5}\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ of the store's chiral-loop convention the two exchange), an anti-Hermitian against a Hermitian bilinear. But $e_{5}$ is the unit Stelle-West direction, unsoldered by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}(i) and pure gauge by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}; so either a coupling to it can be physical, in which case Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} is being read too strongly in Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}(iii), or it cannot, in which case the mirror sector is observationally identical to this one at every level the series reaches. The note takes the second reading, consistently with Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}, and records the operator as the one place the first reading would show; the Hermiticity statement depends on a Dirac-representation convention the note does not fix.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-what-note-de:
The note makes no prediction; no observation can refute its identifications, and the only observational input it uses is the sign of $\Lambda$, which selects which branch describes this universe (Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.what-says-what-it-does-not}). What it claims is a set of identifications, each proved in the note from imported results, and this section says which imported result each identification depends on and what falls with it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(D1)] \emph{The frozen point.} Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}, Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} and all of the section “The soldering decides”, the section “Running the transport on the wall”, the section “Two negative results” and the section “The wall in the cosmological constant” rest on the dark-energy paper's frozen point (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}): the parallel scale tractor of norm $\Lambda/3$ with the Stelle-West vector as the fifth direction of $I^{\perp}$. Without it the algebra of the section “The frozen point splits the ascent's pair” is a statement about an arbitrary vector of the rung's hyperbolic plane with no physical referent.
\item[(D2)] \emph{The soldered residue.} Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower} and Corollaries \claimref{odd-extensions.two-readings-which-which} and \claimref{odd-extensions.not-coupling-between-towers} rest on the dark-matter paper's definition of the residue as the signature of the tangent image (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}). A definition admitting unsoldered directions into the residue would reopen both questions the section closes and, by the same stroke, the exactness of the dark-matter paper's superselection.
\item[(D3)] \emph{The copy theorem's inputs.} Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot} and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(ii) rest on every input of the copy theorem being a spin-group object (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.one-operator-sees-difference}'s conclusion that the mirror sector is observationally identical to this one rests on Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}: a derived quantity depending on the bare fifth generator would need a physical coupling to the pure-gauge direction, which that Fact excludes.
\item[(D4)] \emph{The Goldstone proposition.} Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}(iii) rests on the dark-energy paper's $(I,V)$ sector being pure gauge (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}); a dynamical fixing of the dilation gauge would make the ratio $b/a$ physical.
\item[(D5)] \emph{The residue of a conformal class.} Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.holographic-coincidence}'s statement that the boundary of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ has residue $7$ and lies in a tower distinct from the bulk's rests on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}, on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, and on the signature of a conformal class being well defined. A definition of the residue requiring a chosen scale would withdraw it, and with it the remark's statement of the difference between the two frameworks.
\item[(D6)] \emph{The sheaf paper's hypotheses.} the section “The wall in the cosmological constant” rests on the sheaf paper's tameness conditions and conservation theorem as stated (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue}); its one observation is about the hypothesis of that theorem and stands or falls with the theorem's statement.
\end{enumerate}

__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-adds-dark-energ: The dark-energy paper proves the parabolic-to-reductive rotation of the stabiliser at $\Lambda \neq 0$ at the level of groups. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} is the same rotation at the level of the Clifford algebra: the null direction of the parabolic case is the nilpotent generator of a degenerate algebra, and the reductive case is that generator given a sign. That the tangent image keeps signature $(1,3)$ whatever $\Lambda$ does is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iv) read through Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-says-what-it-do: The de Sitter algebra of this world is two copies of this world, and the anti-de Sitter algebra of this world is this world merged with its mirror, with the mirror sitting on the momenta. This is a statement about the fibrewise Clifford algebra of $I^{\perp}$, which Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} supplies; it is not a statement that a negative cosmological constant would turn matter into mirror matter. The tower charge is soldered and superselected (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses-two-time} below shows that no path of sign changes at fixed dimension four connects the two oriented towers without passing through a sterile signature. What the proposition does establish is that the sign of $\Lambda$ selects which of two non-isomorphic algebras the frozen point's translation generators live in, and that only one of them contains the mirror. The observed cosmological constant is positive \cite{Planck2018}, so the algebra realised in this universe is the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ with no copy of the mirror in it; the mirror on the momenta is a statement about the other sign. The same source gives the present Hubble rate as exceeding the asymptotic rate $\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(ii) by the factor $\Omega_{\Lambda}^{-1/2}$.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.no-mechanism: Together with Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue} this closes the question of a physical passage between the oriented towers within the series: the tower charge is superselected by the one metric, the only algebra in which both towers are present identifies them by the complex unit and not by any automorphism (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.mirror-inside-complexified-extension-absent-doubled}(iv)), and the only continuous route through signatures at dimension four runs through a signature with no causal structure. The two towers share gravity, and by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} the sign of $\Lambda$; that is the whole of the shared channel.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-copies-are: the section “What a single generator does” to the section “The rung's even subalgebra is the anti-de Sitter algebra” are about this world's own ascent. The copy of the mirror's algebra that Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point}(ii) finds on the translation bivectors for $\Lambda < 0$ is not the mirror tower, whose vectors are soldered; it is the reason the two oriented towers' intermediate algebras are non-isomorphic (Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot}), and that non-isomorphism is a statement about the two towers' own ascents under their own solderings, unaffected by this section. Likewise the odd towers' algebras that Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers} finds among the four extensions are their abstract algebras only.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.added-axis-pseudosca: In the doubled case the fifth generator is nothing new: on each summand it acts as the pseudoscalar $\omega' = e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$ of the shadow, up to sign, so the extra space direction of $\Cl(1,4)$ is the chirality operator of $\Cl(1,3)$ promoted from a $4$-blade to a vector, with the choice of sign the only datum the extension adds. In the complexified case the fifth generator is $e_{5} = \pm\,\omega\,\omega'^{-1}$, where the central pseudoscalar $\omega$ ($\omega^{2} = -1$) is the unit of the complexification (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}; for this world the extension is $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\omega = \pm I_5$); in the physicists' notation, with their complex unit read as that central pseudoscalar, it is $I_5\gamma_{5}$ for $\gamma_{5} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3} = \omega'$ (square $-1$), and the algebra is the complexified Dirac algebra; with the Hermitian $\gamma_{5} = I_{5}\omega'$ of the store's chiral-loop convention (the unit read as $I_{5}$) it is $\pm\gamma_{5}$ itself, and $I_{5}\gamma_{5} = -\omega'$ is the doubled case's value.

__notes__.note.odd-extensions.abstract: The transport adds a null pair and climbs a tower without changing its residue. This note asks what a single added generator does to the oriented towers $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(3,1)$. A space-sign generator doubles the shadow, $\Cl(1,4) \cong \Cl(1,3) \oplus \Cl(1,3)$; a time-sign generator complexifies it, $\Cl(2,3) \cong \Cl(1,3) \otimes \C$, and there the mirror's algebra sits, on the anti-de Sitter translation bivectors. The first rung's even subalgebra is $\Cl(2,3)$, so the dark-matter paper's copy theorem runs inside the complexification that forgets the real form; the odd extension is the first construction above the shadow, by dimension, that keeps the towers apart, through an element no derived quantity uses. The dark-energy paper's frozen point realises the extension: its scale tractor and Stelle-West vector are the ascent's pair, signed by $\Lambda$, and the algebra of $I^{\perp}$ is the intermediate of this world's own ascent, $\Cl(1,4)$ for the observed $\Lambda > 0$, $\Cl(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, degenerate at $\Lambda = 0$. By the soldered residue that algebra is this tower's, so $\Lambda$ does not supply the coupling the dark towers need. Run on the degenerate case, the transport returns the rung and a canonical null frame and constrains the frozen point only through its norm: within the series $\Lambda$ is undetermined, its frame components are gauge, and its sign does not select the visible tower. The family over the $\Lambda$ line is a tame wall, completed on both sides in the case the sheaf paper's conservation theorem excludes. The note is a dictionary between three papers, with one new result and no prediction.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-setting-what: Throughout, $\Cl(p,q)$ is the real Clifford algebra on $p$ generators squaring to $+1$ and $q$ squaring to $-1$, $n = p + q$, with orthonormal generators $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{n}$ and volume element $\omega = e_{1}e_{2}\cdots e_{n}$. The series' convention is time $= $ plus: this world is $\Cl(1,3)$, residue $p - q \equiv 6 \pmod 8$, and its mirror is $\Cl(3,1)$, residue $2$. Under the opposite convention every attribution below to a named member of a reversal pair passes to the other member, and the pair-level statements are unchanged; the dark-matter paper carries the same clause \cite[Thm.~3.4]{ButlerT14}. Nothing in this note depends on which member is called this world except the names.
__notes__.note.tower.odd-charge-settled: The odd-charge question of the tower paper (\claimref{q.tower.odd-charge}) is settled by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-limit-forgets-residue}: for every $(p,q)$, with $p - q$ of either parity, the algebraic limit of the tower over $\Cl(p,q)$ is $\Cl(\R^{p,q} \perp H_{\infty}) \cong \Mat_{2^{\infty}}$; for $p - q$ odd it is $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^{\infty}}$, again a plain tensor product, and not $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^{\infty}}$. The limit determines neither $n = p + q$ nor the residue, so no invariant, real K-theoretic or other, of the limit algebra separates the cases. Where the paper's running text calls the odd-charge limit open, or says that the real limit remembers strictly more than the even case, it predates this theorem; the text is kept as the paper wrote it.
__notes__.note.tower.what-completion-means-here-wh: A limit statement must say which completion is meant: here no hidden choice is made. On the algebraic limit the C*-norm is unique (Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}: each stage finite-dimensional, UHF at the top), so ``the completed tower'' is unambiguous once complexified; the real algebraic limit itself is Theorem \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge}, with no completion needed. What is genuinely a choice is the complexification, made because the CAR algebra and its Fock adjointness are complex notions; the real limit remembers strictly more (its real K-theory), which is part of what Question \claimref{q.tower.odd-charge} is about.
__notes__.note.rungs.abstract: The Standard-Model paper of the series needs one hypothesis for the lepton doublet, the singlet listing and its unifying group: that the composite's state space is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$, three pair modes and two slot modes. This note asks whether the tower derives it. The exact part: the spinor module of the $n$-rung transport $\Cl(2,4) \to \Cl(2{+}n, 4{+}n)$ is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{n})$, so the hypothesis says that a two-twistor composite lives two rungs up; the rung-and-pair mixings are $U(n) \times U(3)$ acting as the hypothesis prescribes; the ladder group of the Standard-Model paper is this $U(n)$ on the one-constituent sector; the compact $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is the real form fixed by the tower's adjoint structure once its frames are fixed; and the mass bracket of the mass paper is the frozen point's grip, at $\Lambda = 0$, on the slot-antisymmetric bivector. Given these and the identification of slots with rungs, the rung and slot-statistics hypotheses are one hypothesis in two languages. The part that does not close: no theorem of the series makes each twistor a rung. One completion transports every null momentum at once; the null bivectors of any number of twistors invite one further rung, together, and that rung's $U(2)$ mixes chirality; and the module holds the composite's tuple as one vector, not two twistors. So the hypothesis is sharpened to one structural sentence with a named missing mechanism and, failing that, registered at Tier C with priced kill conditions. Every identity is verified exactly by a deposited script.
__notes__.note.rungs.setting-setting-what-imported: Notation is T12's \cite{ButlerT12}: the pair space $W$, three-dimensional and maximal isotropic in the complexified ambient space $V_{\C}$ of $\Cl(2,4)$; the Dirac module $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ with chirality halves $\T = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ (twistors) and $\T' = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$; the automorphism group $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ with its $U(1)$ factor $(\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$; abelian weight $q$ and hypercharge $Y = q/6$. Hypothesis (S) of T12 is: the composite's state space is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$, with $(A, B)$ acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ and chirality the parity of the total mode number. Eight imports.
__notes__.note.rungs.compact-form: The ambient signature at rung two is $(4,6)$, whose spin group is the noncompact $\mathrm{Spin}(4,6)$; the group in Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3) is the compact $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. They are two real forms of one complex group sharing the module, and the compact one is the real form fixed by the $*$-structure of the tower (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), under which the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$: that adjointness is the Hermitian structure of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, and the Bogoliubov group preserving it is the compact one. The $*$-structure is defined once the tower's frames are fixed, as T3 fixes them, so "fixed by" means fixed given the frames, a choice of maximal compact subgroup made once for the whole series rather than a consequence of the relations alone. The pattern is already present one rung down, where the ambient real form is the conformal $SU(2,2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}) while the pair-mixing group is the unitary group $U(3)$ of $W$ for the same adjointness, inside the compact three-mode Bogoliubov group. A grand-unification group must be compact, and the tower supplies the compact form for the same reason it supplies $U(3)$.
__notes__.note.rungs.where-leaves-r: Three things are now exact that were not. The five-mode ledger is the tower's two-rung module, so (S) is a statement about the tower. The ladder group is the rung-mixing group on the one-constituent sector. And the mass bracket is the frozen point's grip on the slot-antisymmetric bivector, at $\Lambda = 0$, which is a null vector of the ambient space that invites the next rung. What is missing is a single mechanism: why a conformal spinor constituent (a twistor) occupies a rung. The count is the obstacle. Null momenta invite one rung in total (Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}); the bivectors of two conformal spinors invite one more, together (Proposition \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}); neither gives one rung per constituent, and the second gives the right vector space with a $U(2)$ that mixes chirality. The precise form of the missing statement is this: the composite's internal algebra is generated by $3 + n$ anticommuting mode pairs, the three pairs of $W$ shared and one new pair per constituent. Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung} then supplies everything else, the module, the grading and the groups. Why a conformal spinor constituent should contribute exactly one mode to the composite, rather than none (the tensor ledger of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}, where the slots are labels and the pairs are shared) or three (a copy of $W$ per constituent, the product state that Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector} excludes), is the question, and the note has no argument for it. It belongs to the tower paper, where the mode count is a theorem about the real Witt index and where a statement about what a conformal spinor constituent contributes to a composite's algebra would have to be made.
__notes__.note.rungs.setting-position-series: This note is a companion to T12 of the series, alongside a companion note on the lepton, which asks whether the lepton is derivable inside the two-level hierarchy and answers no. \emph{It relies on:} the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the rungs, the Fock module and the Witt index (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), and the transport principle paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the totality and minimality of the completion (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion}); the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the spinor identification, the Witt data and the line at infinity (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}); the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} for the two-twistor mass formula (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-mass-symplectic-area}); and the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the ladder, the automorphism group, Hypothesis (S), the derived generation, the constituent hypothesis of its successor problem (6), and the results priced in the section “The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise” (Facts \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}, \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}). \emph{Papers that would rely on it:} T12, if (R) replaces (S) as the premise or is derived; the tower paper T3, if the missing statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.where-leaves-r} is taken up there, where it belongs; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17}, which would record (S) as a registered premise with the kill conditions of the section “The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise”.
__notes__.note.rungs.setting-fallback-s-tier-c-pre:
If the missing statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.where-leaves-r} is not supplied, the series' own rule for a structural premise that resists derivation is to register it at Tier C, with its predictions and its kill conditions priced. The registration, in the form T12 uses for its stances:

\begin{quote}
\emph{Registered premise (S), equivalently (R).} The internal state space of the minimal massive composite is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$, the two-rung transport of the twistor completion, with the gauge group below the intermediate scale acting through Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) on its determinant-one part (the thirteenth generator, anomaly-free in the action the state space carries, being broken at that scale, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}) and chirality the parity of the mode number.
\end{quote}

\noindent\emph{What it predicts.} (i) Exactly one generation per composite, the sixteen of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$: quark and lepton doublets, four singlets, the fourth at hypercharge zero (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); that the composite carries no further chiral state is the registration's own reading of "the state space is this Fock space", not a clause of Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}. (ii) The $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice of T12 Theorem 4.2; this is unconditional in T12 and is not a test of (S), and is listed because (S) must respect it and does (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}). (iii) Unification into $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ with $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$ at the unification scale, hence, with the desert dead (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}), a change in the running between the weak and unification scales: partner-like content, or an intermediate symmetry such as T12's Pati-Salam route, on which $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ is an input. (iv) Baryon and lepton number violation by the thirty-two generators of $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ outside $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ (Proposition \claimref{rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra}): twelve that move an excitation between a rung and a pair (the leptoquark directions of $\uu(5)$), and twenty that create or annihilate two modes at once.

\noindent\emph{What kills it.} (a) A confirmed chiral fermion outside the sixteen per generation, or a fourth colour singlet with nonzero hypercharge (the anomaly conditions would then admit a family, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}). (b) A fractionally charged colour singlet, off the lattice; this kills the exclusion stance of T12 Theorem 4.2 whether or not (S) holds, so it is a kill shared with T12, not one that discriminates (S). (c) A measured $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ at a scale where the three couplings can be shown, with the observed spectrum plus any partner content compatible with the sixteen, not to meet: the two-loop run with thresholds, T12 successor problem (2). (d) A proton lifetime bound incompatible with any $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ breaking scale allowed by (iii); the framework does not yet fix that scale, so this condition is priced as inherited from the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ literature rather than sharpened. (e) Internally: a proof that the composite's internal algebra closes on the three pair modes alone, with the slots as labels (the tensor ledger reading of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}), which would refute (R) directly and leave (S) without its only structural reading.

\noindent\emph{Level.} A structural premise with priced kill conditions is Tier C by the series' definition; T12 is declared Tier B, and if (S) is registered rather than derived the sections that rest on it (T12 Proposition 5.3(2), Theorem 5.5(1), the consistency clause of (3), the last clause of Proposition 5.6, Proposition 5.8, Remark 5.9, and Proposition 6.1's values $3/8$ and $3/4$, which are taken over a generation containing the lepton; without the lepton the ratio is $9/26$) carry Tier C and the abstract should say so. The sections that do not rest on it, the algebra, the global form, the converse, the quark doublet, the singlet spectrum as a computation on the single-twistor Fock space, the uniqueness arithmetic given a charge list, the trace ratios as arithmetic over any tabulated content with $9/10$ over the fibre, and the run, stay at Tier B.

the nullity of all six pairwise bivectors of a four-twistor instance, and, on the four-mode space, the twisted ground generators generating $\mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$ with the rung's $\{1, v, w, vw\}$ as commutant, $v, w$ anticommuting with chirality and the even part abelian (Proposition \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}; the script's twisted generators square to $-1$, so this verifies the complexified statement, not Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}'s real isomorphism); the absent $\bar{6}$ weights (Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector}); What the script does not check: the Facts beyond the instances named, verified in their own papers' scripts; the real-form statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.compact-form}, which is representation theory imported through Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}; and Hypothesis (R), which is not a computation.
__notes__.note.scrambling.prediction-restated:
Propositions \claimref{scrambling.exact-factorisation-thinning} to \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter} reduce the calibration to the form
\[
N_{\mathrm{epoch}} \;=\; \kappa_c \times (\text{horizon-normalised sphere cells}) \times (\text{one tick per modular period}),
\]
with the normalisation narrowed to two cutoff-free scales by exactness ($r_h$, or $r_* = M$, Proposition \claimref{scrambling.exactness-excludes-cutoff-dependence}), one tick per period being (IC) read as a counting rule, and $\kappa_c$ the residue. The residue is not an artefact of the counting conventions: the chain from tower to count carries no hidden factor of two (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.pair-mode-qubit-one-object}); the helicity clause is closed at the tier of the lift's modelling joint J3 (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(iv), Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-collars-coframe-exceptional-set-helicity}), not at theorem tier; and in the one convention with physical content the residue is $1/(4\ln 2)$, which no recount of the exceptional set with a rational residue ($k = 0$) produces, and, conditionally on the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$, no recount with $k \neq 0$ either (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter}). The prediction's declared form is therefore: \emph{the boundary mode space registers one mode per Bekenstein-Mukhanov area quantum of horizon per modular period}, $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in the capacity convention, and deriving that is equivalent to deriving Bekenstein-Hawking's quarter. Arithmetically $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$ in the 1-nat convention is horizon normalisation replaced by normalisation at $r_* = r_h/2 = M$, since $4\pi M^2 = \SBH$; whether that radius means anything is not decided here. The $16\pi$ of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} stands as the convention-dependent form of the same statement.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-modules-mass: the section “The partner sector quantified” ends with a structural question: what sets a slot-mode mass apart from a pair-mode mass. This section computes what the series' own mass mechanism does on the state space, in the language in which the state space is exact, the two-rung module of the transport tower, whose spinor module is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$ with slots as rungs and pairs as the conformal completion's own null pairs. The mechanism is the mass paper's: mass is coupling to the frozen point, the parallel scale tractor, and the mass of a composite is the length of its grip on that point. The findings, in order: the grip is insensitive to the slots and splits the $5$ inversely (the section “The frozen point is insensitive to the slots”); nothing else derived in the series supplies the split, and the question is the origin of the Higgs doublet (the section “What is and is not derived in the series” and the section “The two flags, resolved”); the doublet's representation is carried by the directions transport adjoined, and a vector in them has exactly the Standard Model's Yukawa pattern (the section “The vector of the module, and the Yukawa pattern”); the frozen point, carried into the completion by the founding construction, lands in those directions (the section “The frozen point, transported”); and, on the same one-generation module, three no-go theorems say what the pattern cannot do, the second family's factor three included (the section “What the pattern cannot do: three no-go theorems”). Everything below that uses the state space is conditional on Hypothesis (S), and each result that names a species of the generation says so in its statement; notation follows the mass paper. Seven imports and one definition carry the argument.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-what-algebra-fixes-wh: The tower theorems are kinematic: they fix the algebraic setting, not the physics within it. Fixed by the algebra alone: the mode count and its capacity bound (Theorem \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}); the Fock module and its qubit-per-rung doubling (Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}); the matrix-unit description of ascent and descent, including the one-way pinching of \cite[\S7.3]{ButlerT1}; and the CAR limit as the algebra in which a mode continuum lies (Theorem \claimref{tower.car-limit-even-charge}). Not fixed by the algebra: which state the field algebra carries. Thermality of a mode, entanglement across a ladder pair, the thermofield-double structure of a horizon pair, and everything downstream of a choice of vacuum are properties of states on the CAR factor, constrained but not selected by the kinematics established here. That division is deliberate: T5 \cite{ButlerT5} computes a specific transport chain in a specific state and shows where its information goes; this paper certifies that the algebra it computes in is the canonical one, with its capacity count exact. The reading of modular theory on a single mode, and its extension over the limit as free-fermion thermal field theory, is T5's task; here it is a reference, not a claim.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-car-limit: The limit theorem compares the tower not with itself but with its image under the identifications $\varphi_k$ of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, and the corrector must be computed \emph{after} that transport. The next lemma does so; the answer differs from the single-step corrector.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-scope: Algebra-level theorems, proved here: rigidity (Theorems \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, \claimref{tower.rigidity-clock-frozen}), the CAR relations and Fock modules (Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}, Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}), capacity (Theorem \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}), the even-charge limit (Theorems \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge}, \claimref{tower.car-limit-even-charge}). Imported theorems: the single step and its minimality \cite{ButlerT1}; the wall sequence \cite{ButlerT4}. Open, stated as such: the odd-charge limit (Question \claimref{q.tower.odd-charge}). Physical readings, flagged as readings: ``one qubit per rung'' as a statement about horizon or singularity modes (the algebra supplies the register; identifying its qubits with counted physical modes is the task of the series' counting papers); ``iterated transport is second quantisation'' as a slogan (the theorem is the tensor factorisation with CAR; the slogan adds an interpretive claim about what quantisation is that the mathematics neither needs nor decides).
__notes__.note.tower.setting-machine-verification: Every computational identity in this paper has been checked by computer, in exact rational arithmetic over the shared library's basis-blade Clifford product, in the manner of the verifications deposited with \cite{ButlerT1, ButlerT4}. The script \texttt{verify\_T03.py}, deposited with this paper alongside the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py}, \cite{ButlerVerifyT03}, performs its checks and reports each. The coverage: the volume-element lemma in full on the two-rung floor over $\Cl(1,3)$ (squares, own-plane anticommutation, all cross commutations, and the $\Omega_2$ properties); the commuting-copies theorem at $k = 2$, where the twisted generators are verified to satisfy the ground relations, all sixteen generator pairs of $A_2$ against $B_2$ commute, and the $256$ products of $A$-blades with $B$-blades are checked to be $256$ \emph{distinct} basis blades of $\Cl(3,5)$, an exact generation-and-dimension count; the frozen clock on floors $0$, $1$, $2$ of the physical tower by exhaustive blade-wise commutant (valid for diagonal forms, where an element is central exactly when each blade of its support is), each centre coming out $\operatorname{span}\{1\}$, so no checked floor hosts a central idempotent; the twenty-seven CAR relations of three ladder pairs in $\Cl(3,3)$ as vector identities; the Fock module on $\Lambda^\bullet W_3$ (the anticommutators on all eight states, $c(\alpha)^2 = Q(\alpha)\,\mathrm{id}$ for a general rational vector, the vacuum clause, and irreducibility by the exact rank of the sixty-four blade actions inside $\End(\Lambda^\bullet W_3)$); capacity instances in $\Cl(2,4)$ and on the floor $\Cl(3,5)$, with the isotropy and independence (exact rank) of the creation span verified in both algebras, as in the theorem's own argument; the grade twist: $\Ad_u$ equal to the grade involution on all blades of $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(2,4)$, the block conjugation $U \operatorname{diag}(a,a)\,U^{-1} = \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$ in $\Mat_2(\Cl(1,3))$, and the odd-charge outerness witnessed in $\Cl(1,0)$ (commutative, yet the involution swaps its central idempotents); the compatibility lemma in full at one stage over the ground algebra $\Cl(1,1)$, where the transported connecting map is checked against $\Ad(V_k) \circ \theta_k$ with the \emph{split} corrector of Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported}, generator by generator inside $\Cl(3,3)$, and the naive corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_1})$ is checked to fail, so the split is necessary; the *-structure of Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} on $\Cl(2,2)$ (antimultiplicativity on sampled products, unitarity of all generators and of the volume elements, and $v^* = w$ for the ladder pair); and the single-step corrector identity of Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner} rearranged as one commuting square, on a sample element. Thirty-one checks in all. No floating point is used anywhere; the script exits nonzero on any failure, and all checks pass.
__notes__.note.tower.eight-towers-signature-change: The eight clock positions classify not stages of one tower but eight parallel towers, one per transport charge. The two sides of a tame signature-change wall carry charges $d$ and $d - 2$ \cite[\S 7.2]{ButlerT4}, and the shadow wall, where the two competing completions conflict, is where two towers of different charge meet. The wall sequence of \cite[Cor.~5.5]{ButlerT4} is a sequence of such meetings between neighbouring towers, displaced rung by rung away from the physical region.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-car-limit-2: Completing in a C*-norm presupposes a *-structure, and a proof must state which one is meant; the tower carries a canonical one, determined by its frames.
__notes__.note.tower.abstract: The transport principle of this series completes $\Cl(p,q)$ to $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$; the completed algebra carries a null cone of its own, so the completion invites iteration. This paper settles what the iterated tower is. Rigidity first: $\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$ canonically, so the transport charge $p - q$ is constant along the tower and the mod-8 clock never ticks. Bott periodicity manifests not as eventual return but as immediate freeze: every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor, and the eight clock positions classify eight parallel towers rather than stages of one. Each rung adjoins one hyperbolic plane, and the adjoined ladder pairs satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations exactly, as vectors: the tower is a fermionic register, one mode per rung, with Fock modules doubling at every floor and the Witt index counting capacity. The limit theorem settles the second-quantisation question: for even transport charge the grade twist in the connecting embeddings is inner by Skolem and Noether, the algebraic direct limit is $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$, and the completed complexified limit is the ground algebra tensored with the CAR algebra of countably many fermionic modes. Iterated transport is second quantisation. The odd-charge case, where the twist acts on the centre, is delimited precisely and posed. The paper is pure mathematics: complete proofs throughout, with the handful of imported classical results stated as facts carrying their provenance. Every computational identity is verified in exact arithmetic in an accompanying script.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-introduction:
The root paper of the series \cite{ButlerT1} repairs the failure of division at the null cone of $\Cl(p,q)$ by the minimal Witt completion $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$, shows this is one of exactly two transport rules, classifies what each adjoins, and proves that the completed algebra is the matrix amplification $\Mat_2(\Cl(p,q))$ with the base embedded as a twisted diagonal. The completed algebra, being a Clifford algebra of mixed signature, has a null cone of its own. The question this paper answers is the evident one: what happens when the transport is iterated? Three specific forms of the question: does the ascended algebra's own singular behaviour force a further ascent, without end; does the mod-8 periodicity of the real Clifford classification make the climb circulate; and what is the limit object?

The answers are more specific than the questions. The tower $\Cl(p{+}k,q{+}k)$ is canonically $\Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$, so the climb never leaves the ground floor's Morita class: the clock is frozen, not circulating, and the eight clock positions classify eight parallel towers, one per transport charge $p - q \bmod 8$, rather than eight stages of one tower. What the iteration accumulates is capacity, not algebraic type: each rung adjoins one hyperbolic plane whose ladder pair satisfies the canonical anticommutation relations exactly, the Fock module doubles, and the Witt index, the algebra's count of independent fermionic modes, increases by exactly one. The limit is then the object the physical reading requires: the ground algebra tensored with the CAR algebra of a free fermionic field. Iterated transport is second quantisation, one mode per rung.

The mathematical content of the limit statement requires operator-algebraic care, which it receives here. The connecting embeddings are twisted diagonals $a \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$, with $\hat a$ the grade involution; whether the twist can be removed decides whether the limit is a plain tensor product. For even transport charge the ground algebra is central simple, the involution is inner by the Skolem-Noether theorem, and the twist conjugates away rung by rung: the algebraic limit is exactly $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$, and its completed complexification is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$. For odd charge the grade involution acts nontrivially on the centre and is outer; the even-charge argument does not apply, and rather than assert the unproved standard expectation we delimit the boundary and pose the odd case precisely.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-prior-art: Every ingredient is classical; the assembly and the transport reading are the contributions. The isomorphism $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1) \cong \Mat_2(\Cl(p,q))$ is the $(1,1)$-periodicity of the real Clifford classification, due in matrix form to the classical structure theory \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001} and in K-theoretic form to Atiyah, Bott and Shapiro \cite{ABS1964}; \cite{ButlerT1} re-derives it directly from the transport construction, with the ladder pair as explicit matrix units, and that derivation is the one iterated here. UHF algebras and their classification are Glimm's \cite{Glimm1960}; AF algebras and their diagrams are Bratteli's \cite{Bratteli1972}; the CAR algebra, its uniqueness, its Fock representations and its identification with the $2^\infty$ UHF algebra are standard operator algebra \cite{BratteliRobinson1997}. The Chevalley construction realising Clifford algebras on exterior algebras of isotropic subspaces \cite{Chevalley1997} is the mechanism behind the Fock module theorem. The Skolem-Noether theorem, the classical frame for the even-charge innerness \cite{Pierce1982}, is not actually imported: the implementing element is exhibited directly. Morita theory is classical \cite{Lam1999}. The infinite wall sequence that makes the far-side iteration unconditional is proved in the sheaf paper of this series \cite{ButlerT4}; the root paper \cite{ButlerT1} supplies the single step and its minimality. The contributions here are the canonical form of the rigidity, the exact CAR relations at vector level, the Skolem-Noether treatment of the grade twist, and the precise odd-charge boundary.
__notes__.note.tower.setting-contribution:
At the standard of \cite{ButlerT1}: complete proofs, each theorem carrying its own hypotheses.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Tower rigidity} (the section “Tower rigidity: the frozen clock”). $\Cl(p{+}k,q{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$ by an isomorphism assembled canonically from the $k$ ladder pairs, with the commuting-copies mechanism made explicit: the base re-embeds as $x \mapsto x\,\omega_1\cdots\omega_k$ against the adjoined planes' volume elements, and the two constructions (nested matrix units, commuting copies) agree. Transport charge is invariant, the clock is frozen, every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor, and no type-C obstruction ever arises by transport from a simple ground algebra.
\item \textbf{Eight towers} (the section “Tower rigidity: the frozen clock”). The mod-8 residues classify parallel towers; a signature-change wall is a meeting of two towers whose charges differ by two, and the shadow-wall phenomenon of \cite{ButlerT4} is re-read as tower change.
\item \textbf{One qubit per rung} (the section “One qubit per rung: Fock modules and capacity”). The adjoined null pairs satisfy the CAR exactly as vectors; the Fock module theorem: the algebra of $k$ adjoined planes acts irreducibly on the exterior algebra of the span of the creation directions, of dimension $2^k$, doubling per rung; and Witt index is quantum capacity: the maximal number of independent fermionic modes an algebra of the tower hosts is exactly its Witt index, which increases by one per rung.
\item \textbf{The CAR limit} (the section “The CAR limit”). For $p - q$ even: the grade involution is inner (Skolem-Noether), the twisted diagonals conjugate to untwisted ones stage by stage, the algebraic direct limit of the tower is $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$ canonically, and the completed complexified limit is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$, the ground algebra tensored with a free fermionic field algebra. For $p - q$ odd the twist is outer on the centre and the question is posed with the obstruction identified.
\item \textbf{What the dynamics demands} (the section “Physical reading, and scope”). Imported from \cite{ButlerT4} and \cite{ButlerT1} and assembled: on the physical closure nothing divides by zero at floor one and no further ascent is dynamically forced; beyond the shadow walls the demand is unconditional and infinite, one rung per wall. The scope section separates algebra-level theorems from physical readings.
\end{enumerate}
__notes__.note.tower.setting-tower-rigidity-frozen: The central construction of the section is a pair of commuting subalgebras that between them generate each floor. The construction is classical in spirit; the form given here keys it to the transport data (the planes and their volume elements), which is what makes the iteration and the limit computation of the section “The CAR limit” exact. a figure of the original displays the object the section is about.
__notes__.note.tower.what-capacity-theorem-forbids: The theorem is a prohibition as much as a count: no choice of vectors extracts $\min(p,q) + k + 1$ fermionic modes from floor $k$. Capacity is quantified by the Witt index, the same quantity that the transport rules increment; the reading of the increment as ``one qubit per rung'' is therefore an exact identity, not an analogy. (Mode systems built from non-vector elements are a different question, deliberately outside the theorem's hypotheses; at vector level the count is sharp.)

dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-.formal: The (1,1) ascent preserves $p - q$ and $\Cl(p+k, q+k) \cong \Mat(2^{k}, \Cl(p,q))$ (Bott), so the eight residues label eight parallel towers. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~3.2, 3.6, Rem.~3.7]{ButlerT3}, \cite[\S7]{ButlerT1}.
dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-.technical:
The $(1,1)$ ascent $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p+1,q+1)$ adjoins one hyperbolic plane, so it leaves $p - q$ unchanged, and iterating it gives $\Cl(p+k, q+k) \cong \Mat(2^{k}, \Cl(p,q))$, the Bott-type matrix doubling. The residue $p - q \bmod 8$ is therefore constant along each chain of ascents, and the eight residues label eight parallel towers.

In the store this fact restates the commuting-copies theorem and the rigidity of the clock along the tower.
dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-.lay: Climbing the ladder of algebras by adding one plus-square direction and one minus-square direction never changes the difference between the two counts. Each step replaces the algebra by two-by-two matrices with entries in the old one, so nothing essential changes. The possible starting points therefore sort into eight separate towers, according to that difference counted modulo eight.

hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-.formal: For even transport charge, the completed complexified limit of the tower of iterated completions is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$, the ground algebra tensored with the CAR algebra of countably many fermionic modes, and the mode operators are the adjoined null pairs themselves ($a_j = v_j^* = w_j$, $a_j^\dagger = v_j$, with the Fock adjointness). Here the \emph{transport charge} is the mod-8 invariant $p - q \bmod 8$, which the tower's completions preserve and the \emph{lineage} is the tower of iterated completions itself, both as in \cite{ButlerT3}; the physical lineage has charge six, so the theorem applies. \emph{Provenance:} the tower paper \cite[Prop.~4.1, Thms.~5.3 and 5.6]{ButlerT3}.
hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-.technical:
For even transport charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$, the tower of iterated completions $\Cl(p+k,q+k)$, complexified and completed in its C*-norm, has limit $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$: the ground algebra tensored with the CAR algebra of countably many fermionic modes. The complexification is the tower's own: $\C$ is read as $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ in a tensor factor, its unit $1 \otimes I_4$ central and not an element of any floor (Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}).

The mode operators are the adjoined null pairs themselves, $a_j = v_j^* = w_j$ and $a_j^\dagger = v_j$, with the adjointness of the Fock module. The physical lineage has charge six, which is even, so the result applies to it.
hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-.lay: Each step of the series' completion adds one fermionic mode. Taking infinitely many steps, for towers of even charge, produces the algebra of a free fermion field with countably many modes, attached to the original algebra. Our world's tower has charge six, so the result covers it; the Hawking paper takes these modes of the tower as its boundary modes.

obj.odd-extensions.single-extension.formal: The \emph{time extension} of $\Cl(p,q)$ is $\Cl(p+1, q)$ and its \emph{space extension} is $\Cl(p, q+1)$, each with the new generator written $e_{n+1}$ and the old generators, and the subalgebra they generate, called the \emph{shadow}. A single extension is not a transport in the series' sense: the transport adjoins a null pair $e_{+} + e_{-}$ because a zero divisor of vector type is resolved by a nilpotent, and a single generator squaring to $\pm 1$ supplies none \cite[\S 8]{ButlerT1}.
obj.odd-extensions.single-extension.technical:
Given $\Cl(p,q)$, its time extension is $\Cl(p+1,q)$ and its space extension is $\Cl(p,q+1)$: one new generator $e_{n+1}$ is adjoined, and the old generators, together with the subalgebra they generate, are called the shadow.

A single extension is not a transport in the series' sense. The transport adjoins a null pair built from $e_+$ and $e_-$, because a zero divisor of vector type is resolved by a nilpotent, and a single generator with $Q(e_{n+1}) = \pm 1$ supplies none.
obj.odd-extensions.single-extension.lay: A single extension adds just one new direction to an algebra of directions, either of time type or of space type, and the original algebra survives inside it as its shadow. This differs from the series' basic completion step, which adds two directions at once so as to supply a direction of zero length. One new direction on its own cannot do that.

obj.tower.tower.formal: The \emph{tower} over $\Cl(p,q)$ is the chain of algebras $T_k := \Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k)$, $k \geq 0$, on the spaces $\R^{p,q} \perp H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$ with $H_j = \operatorname{span}\{e_j, f_j\}$ orthogonal hyperbolic planes, together with the natural unital embeddings $\iota_k : T_k \hookrightarrow T_{k+1}$ induced by the inclusion of quadratic spaces. Write $v_j, w_j$ for the $j$-th null pair, $\omega_j := e_j f_j$ for the $j$-th plane's volume element, and $d := p - q \bmod 8$ for the \emph{transport charge}.
obj.tower.tower.technical:
The tower over $\Cl(p,q)$ is the chain of algebras $T_k = \Cl(p+k, q+k)$, $k \geq 0$, built on $\R^{p,q} \perp H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$, where each $H_j = \operatorname{span}\{e_j, f_j\}$ is a hyperbolic plane orthogonal to the others, together with the unital embeddings $\iota_k : T_k \hookrightarrow T_{k+1}$ induced by the inclusion of quadratic spaces.

Each plane carries a null pair $v_j, w_j$ and a volume element $\omega_j = e_j f_j$, and the transport charge of the tower is $d = p - q \bmod 8$.
obj.tower.tower.lay: The tower is the ladder of algebras obtained by repeatedly adding a pair of new directions, one of each sign, at right angles to everything before. Each algebra sits naturally inside the next. Each added pair can be recombined into two directions of zero length, and the difference between the numbers of the two kinds of direction, counted modulo eight, is the tower's charge.

odd-extensions.belongs-tower.technical:
Read the residue of a sector, as the imported copy theorem does, as the signature of its soldered vector space: the image of the tangent space in the algebra, with $Q(v) = g(v,v)$. For the frozen point's algebra $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ the soldered space is the Lorentz frame $\{I,V\}^{\perp} = e(TM)$, of signature $(1,3)$ for every $\Lambda$, and the Stelle-West vector $V$ lies outside it. Hence $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ has tower charge $6$: it is a sub-object of this world's rung, not the ground shadow of the residue-$5$ or residue-$7$ tower whose abstract algebra it shares.

For $\Lambda > 0$ the isomorphism $\Cl(I^{\perp}) \cong \Cl(1,4)$ comes from an isometry of quadratic spaces but from no map of soldered data. Under the premise of one four-dimensional metric (P1), the isometry sends the unsoldered $e_V$ to a fifth tangent direction of a five-dimensional shadow and the four-dimensional soldered space into a proper subspace of that shadow's tangent space.
odd-extensions.belongs-tower.lay: The algebra attached to the frozen point looks, as bare algebra, like the algebra of a five-dimensional dark tower. But under the reading the paper imports, which assigns towers by which directions are genuinely tied to spacetime, this algebra's tied directions are just the four ordinary spacetime directions. Assuming, as Premise P1 does, that there is one four-dimensional metric, its fifth direction is not a spacetime direction, so the algebra belongs to our own tower and not to a dark one.
odd-extensions.belongs-tower.typing_note: Added the copy-theorem fact, named in the statement as the reading of the residue the result works under, and assumed Premise P1, which the proof of (iii) invokes by name; kept the projection lemma, whose sourcing-rule reading of P1 supplies the shared four directions beyond which a fifth tangent direction is internal. Levels pass: the lay level and one-liner now state Premise P1 and the imported reading of the residue; the technical level names P1.

proofs.main: (i) is Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} with Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iv). (ii) The residue is the signature of the soldered space by definition (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and that signature is $(1,3)$, residue $6$; the algebra generated by the soldered space together with the unsoldered $e_{V}$ lies inside the rung generated by the soldered space together with the ascent's pair. (iii) A five-dimensional shadow of residue $5$ is, by the same definition, an algebra whose soldered space has signature $(1,4)$, so all five generators are tangent; under the one four-dimensional metric of the dark-matter paper's Premise P1 (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}) this needs a fifth tangent direction beyond the four, an internal direction in the sense of that paper's projection lemma \cite[Lem.~6.1]{ButlerT14} (\claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}). The isometry $I^{\perp} \cong \R^{1,4}$ identifies $e_{V}$ with that direction, so it does not carry the soldered space onto the soldered space, which is what the dark-matter paper's Theorem 3.5(i) requires of a map that preserves the residue.

odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-def.formal: The intermediate algebra of this world's ascent is a one-parameter family in $\Lambda$: the degenerate $\Cl(1,3;1)$ at $\Lambda = 0$, whose nilpotent generator is the zero divisor the transport is built to resolve, deformed to the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and the complexified $\Cl(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$. The sign of $\Lambda$ fixes the sign given to the ascent's null generator (the generator's square is $-\Lambda/3$, the opposite sign), and the two odd extensions are the two ways of giving it one.
odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-def.technical:
The intermediate algebra of this world's ascent is a one-parameter family in $\Lambda$. At $\Lambda = 0$ it is the degenerate $\Cl(1,3;1)$, whose nilpotent generator is the zero divisor the transport is built to resolve; for $\Lambda > 0$ it deforms to the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ and for $\Lambda < 0$ to the complexified $\Cl(2,3)$.

The ascent's null generator acquires the square $Q = -\Lambda/3$, of sign opposite to $\Lambda$, and the two odd extensions are the two ways of giving it a sign.
odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-def.lay: The cosmological constant controls which algebra sits halfway up our world's completion step. When it is zero, that algebra contains a direction of zero length, exactly the kind of defect the completion exists to cure. A positive or negative value gives that direction a nonzero length of the opposite sign, turning the algebra into one of two different odd-dimensional forms.
odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-def.typing_note: The single use is the theorem whose clauses the proof cites and is kept. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

The ascent's generator in $I^{\perp}$ beyond the Lorentz frame is $d\,e_{+} + c\,e_{-}$, orthogonal to $I$, of square $d^{2} - c^{2} = -\Lambda/3$; at $\Lambda = 0$, where $c = \pm d$, it is $\pm I$, the nilpotent generator. It is this generator whose square the statement gives; $I$ itself has square $+\Lambda/3$.

odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses.formal: At fixed dimension four, a change of the sign of one generator moves the signature $(p, 4-p)$ to $(p \pm 1, 4 - p \mp 1)$ and the residue by $\pm 2$. Every sequence of such changes from $(1,3)$ to $(3,1)$ passes through $(2,2)$, residue $0$, the two-time sterile fork; the other neighbour of $(1,3)$, the Euclidean $(0,4)$ at residue $4$, is a dead end from which the only continuation returns to $(1,3)$.
odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses.technical:
At fixed dimension four the signatures are $(p, 4-p)$ with $p = 0, \ldots, 4$, and changing the sign of one generator moves $p$ by one and the residue $p - q \bmod 8$ by $\pm 2$.

Every sequence of such changes from this world's $(1,3)$ to the mirror's $(3,1)$ passes through $(2,2)$, the residue-$0$ two-time sterile fork. The other neighbour of $(1,3)$, the Euclidean $(0,4)$ at residue $4$, is a dead end whose only continuation returns to $(1,3)$.
odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses.lay: Flipping the sign of one direction at a time, there is no way to get from our spacetime's signature to its mirror image without passing through a signature with two time directions. The only other move from our signature leads to the purely spatial one, and from there the only way out is straight back. So every such route to the mirror goes through the two-time case.
odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses.typing_note: Self-contained combinatorial proof with no premises; no edges needed.

odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-.formal: The residues of the four extensions are $5$, $7$, $1$, $3$ (Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}), and they land on the odd towers in two roles: $\Cl(1,4)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$, this world's space extension and the mirror's time extension, are the representatives at the dimension nearest four of the residues $5$ and $3$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}), the two five-dimensional dark towers; $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\Cl(3,2)$, this world's time extension and the mirror's space extension, are the conformal ambients (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}) of the representatives $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ of the residues $7$ and $1$, the two three-dimensional dark towers. This is a statement about abstract algebras: the frozen point's algebra $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ of Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} coincides with a five-dimensional shadow for $\Lambda > 0$ and with a three-dimensional ambient for $\Lambda < 0$ as an algebra, and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower} says that as a soldered object it is neither.
odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-.technical:
The four single extensions have residues $5, 7, 1, 3$ and land on the four odd towers in two roles. $\Cl(1,4)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$, this world's space extension and the mirror's time extension, are the representatives at the dimension nearest four of residues $5$ and $3$, the two five-dimensional dark towers. $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\Cl(3,2)$, this world's time extension and the mirror's space extension, are the conformal ambients of the representatives $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ of residues $7$ and $1$, the two three-dimensional dark towers.

This is a statement about abstract algebras only. The frozen point's algebra $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ coincides as an algebra with a five-dimensional shadow for $\Lambda > 0$ and with a three-dimensional ambient for $\Lambda < 0$, but as a soldered object it is neither.
odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-.lay: Adding one direction to our spacetime's algebra, or to its mirror's, can be done in four ways, and the four results match, as algebras, the four odd dark towers of the series. Two match the dark towers' own algebras directly and two match them after the one-step conformal enlargement. The matching is purely algebraic: once one tracks which directions belong to spacetime, the frozen point's algebra is none of them.
