synthesis.tower-top-pair-forgets-reversa.formal:
Let $T_{k} = \Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ be the floors of the tower over $\Cl(p,q)$, with ground generators $x_{1}, \dots, x_{n}$ ($n = p + q$, $r = p - q$) and planes $(e_{j}, f_{j})$, $e_{j}^{2} = 1$, $f_{j}^{2} = -1$, $j \ge 1$; let $L_{p,q} = \varinjlim T_{k}$ (the algebraic limit) and $B_{\infty} \subset L_{p,q}$ the subalgebra generated by all plane generators. A pair isomorphism is an algebra isomorphism $\Phi \colon L_{p,q} \to L_{p',q'}$ with $\Phi(B_{\infty}) = B_{\infty}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Reversal.)} Let $y_{1}, \dots, y_{n}$ be the ground generators of the tower over $\Cl(q,p)$, numbered so that $y_{i}^{2} = -x_{i}^{2}$. The assignment
\[
x_{i} \mapsto y_{i}e_{1}, \qquad e_{1} \mapsto e_{1}, \qquad e_{j} \mapsto e_{1}f_{j-1} \ (j \ge 2), \qquad f_{j} \mapsto e_{1}e_{j+1} \ (j \ge 1)
\]
extends to a pair isomorphism $\Phi \colon L_{p,q} \to L_{q,p}$, whose inverse is given by the same formula read from $(q,p)$ to $(p,q)$. It carries $T_{k}$ into $T'_{k+1}$ and $B_{k}$ into $B'_{k+1}$, and $\Phi^{-1}$ carries $T'_{k}$ into $T_{k+1}$; no floor goes onto a floor. On the planes' commutants it is $x_{i}x_{j} \mapsto -y_{i}y_{j}$, the isomorphism $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl^{0}(q,p)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.plane-commutant-even-ground}(iii). $\Phi$ is a $*$-isomorphism for the frame $*$-structure (every generator unitary, Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}), so its complexification extends to an isomorphism of the C*-completions of the limits (Theorem \claimref{tower.car-limit-even-charge} for $p - q$ even) carrying the closure of $B_{\infty}$ onto the closure of $B_{\infty}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Classification of tower-top pairs.)} For $n, n' \ge 1$ the pairs $(L_{p,q}, B_{\infty})$ and $(L_{p',q'}, B_{\infty})$ are isomorphic if and only if $n' = n$ and $r' \equiv \pm r \pmod 8$. For $n \ge 1$ and $n' = 0$ they are never isomorphic, since $B_{\infty}$ is the whole limit when $n' = 0$ and a proper subalgebra when $n \ge 1$. In particular the pair, as an inclusion, does not distinguish $r$ from $-r$: it records exactly what the planes' commutant records.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Where the sign lives, over $\R$.)} Grade the real algebra $L_{p,q}$ by its grade involution $\alpha$. The elements that supercommute with every plane generator are exactly $\Cl(p,q) \subset T_{0}$, so the graded pair $(L_{p,q}, B_{\infty}, \alpha)$ determines $\Cl(p,q)$ up to isomorphism and separates $r$ from $-r$ whenever $r \not\equiv 0, 4 \pmod 8$. The reversal $\Phi$ carries $\alpha$ not to the grade involution $\alpha'$ of $L_{q,p}$ but to $\theta' = \operatorname{Ad}(e_{1}) \circ \alpha'$, the automorphism that negates $e_{1}$ and fixes every other generator, whose implementer has $e_{1}\,\alpha'(e_{1}) = -1$; the supercommutant of the planes for $\theta'$ is the mirror copy generated by the $y_{i}e_{1}$. Over $\R$ the sign of $r$ at the top of the tower is therefore carried by the grading and by nothing in the ungraded pair. After complexification the supercommutant is $\Cl(p,q)_{\C}$, which depends on $n$ alone, so there neither the pair nor the grading carries the sign.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Rule 2 at the tower top.)} For $p - q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ the two repairs $\Cl(p{+}1,q)$ and $\Cl(p,q{+}1)$ of Fact \claimref{rule2.imported-rule-2-matrix-units-forgotten}, isomorphic as algebras, have residues $r + 1$ and $r - 1$, which are never congruent up to sign modulo $8$; so the tower-top pairs built over the two repairs are never isomorphic. The sign of the adjoined generator, which the fused algebra forgets, is recorded by the ungraded tower-top pair, through the planes' commutant (its centre is $\C$ for one repair and $\R \oplus \R$ for the other).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.tower-top-pair-forgets-reversa.technical: The top of the tower over $\Cl(p,q)$ and the top of the tower over the reversed signature $\Cl(q,p)$ are isomorphic even when the plane subalgebra is required to go to itself. The isomorphism multiplies each ground generator by the first plane generator $e_{1}$, which reverses every ground square, and re-pairs the infinitely many plane generators: the elements $e_{1}$ and $e_{1}w$, for $w$ the other plane generators, again form an infinite supply of hyperbolic planes generating the plane algebra. The re-pairing shifts the planes along by one, like a hotel with infinitely many rooms, which is why no finite floor is mapped onto a floor and why the finite floors, which do separate the two signatures, give no obstruction. Together with the even ground algebra already known to sit in the planes' commutant, this classifies tower-top pairs: they are determined by $n$ and the residue up to sign, and the residue's sign is not recorded. Over the reals it is recorded once the grading is part of the data: the elements supercommuting with the planes are then the whole ground algebra, and the reversal isomorphism does not respect the grading. After complexification, as in the store's completed limit, even the grading no longer carries the sign, because the complexified ground algebra depends only on the number of generators. The isomorphism respects the adjoint, so it passes to the C*-completion. The same comparison applied to Rule 2 goes the other way: the two repairs of a split extension are isomorphic algebras, but their towers' tops are not isomorphic pairs.
synthesis.tower-top-pair-forgets-reversa.lay: Every tower of algebras ends at the same top, and the question was whether the way the top is put together, the position of the blocks added on the way up, still remembers whether the tower started from a signature or from its mirror image. It does not. An explicit relabelling, using the infinitely many added blocks to absorb a sign change, carries one top onto the other block for block. The mirror-image information survives only if one also keeps track of which elements count as odd, the grading that the physics of fermions treats as real. So the series' premise that a tower and its mirror are alike is an exact symmetry of the tower top with its plane algebra, and over the real numbers the one thing that tells them apart is the grading.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The algebraic limit $L_{p,q}$ is the union of the floors under the inclusions of generators (\claimref{obj.tower.tower}), that is, the Clifford algebra of the countable-dimensional quadratic space $V \oplus H^{\infty}$ spanned by the ground and plane generators; an assignment of elements to the generators that satisfies the Clifford relations (each image squares to the square of its generator, distinct images anticommute) therefore extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism (\claimref{std-algebra.existence-uniqueness}), floor by floor and hence on the union.

\emph{(i).} Write $Q(g)$ for the square of a generator $g$. Every image is a product of two anticommuting unit generators, except $\Phi(e_{1}) = e_{1}$. For two anticommuting generators $g, h$ of the target, $(gh)^{2} = -g^{2}h^{2}$, so $\Phi(x_{i})^{2} = -y_{i}^{2} = x_{i}^{2}$, $\Phi(e_{j})^{2} = (e_{1}f_{j-1})^{2} = -(1)(-1) = 1$ for $j \ge 2$, and $\Phi(f_{j})^{2} = (e_{1}e_{j+1})^{2} = -1$. For anticommutation: two images $e_{1}g$, $e_{1}h$ with $g \ne h$ distinct from $e_{1}$ satisfy $(e_{1}g)(e_{1}h) = -gh$, whose symmetrisation vanishes; $e_{1}$ anticommutes with every $e_{1}g$, since $e_{1}(e_{1}g) = g = -(e_{1}g)e_{1}$; and $\Phi(x_{i}) = y_{i}e_{1}$ against $e_{1}h$ or $e_{1}$ is the same computation with $y_{i}$ in place of $g$, the right-hand placement of $e_{1}$ changing only an overall sign. The images are pairwise distinct products (the map $g \mapsto$ the second factor is injective onto $\{y_{i}\} \cup \{f_{j-1}\} \cup \{e_{j+1}\}$), so $\Phi$ is an algebra homomorphism $L_{p,q} \to L_{q,p}$. The same formula read from $(q,p)$ to $(p,q)$ defines $\Psi \colon L_{q,p} \to L_{p,q}$, and on generators $\Psi\Phi(x_{i}) = \Psi(y_{i})\Psi(e_{1}) = x_{i}e_{1}e_{1} = x_{i}$, $\Psi\Phi(e_{j}) = e_{1}\cdot e_{1}e_{j} = e_{j}$ ($j \ge 2$), $\Psi\Phi(f_{j}) = e_{1}\cdot e_{1}f_{j} = f_{j}$, and symmetrically $\Phi\Psi = \mathrm{id}$; so $\Phi$ is an isomorphism. The images of plane generators involve plane generators only, so $\Phi(B_{\infty}) \subseteq B_{\infty}$ and likewise $\Psi(B_{\infty}) \subseteq B_{\infty}$, whence $\Phi(B_{\infty}) = B_{\infty}$. The images of the generators of $T_{k}$ use plane indices up to $k+1$, which gives the floor statements; $\Phi(T_{k}) \not\subseteq T'_{k}$ because $\Phi(f_{k}) = e_{1}e_{k+1}$, and $\dim \Phi(T_{k}) = \dim T'_{k} < \dim T'_{k+1}$, so no floor goes onto a floor. Finally $\Phi(x_{i}x_{j}) = y_{i}e_{1}y_{j}e_{1} = -y_{i}y_{j}$. \emph{Completion.} For the frame $*$-structure of Theorem \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}, $g^{*} = g^{-1}$ for every generator. Each $\Phi(g)$ is a product of frame generators, hence unitary, so $\Phi(g)^{*} = \Phi(g)^{-1} = \Phi(g^{-1}) = \Phi(g^{*})$; $\Phi \circ *$ and $* \circ \Phi$ are conjugate-linear antihomomorphisms (after complexification) agreeing on generators, so they agree and $\Phi$ is a $*$-isomorphism. Its restriction $T_{k,\C} \to T'_{k+1,\C}$ is an injective $*$-homomorphism of finite-dimensional C*-algebras, hence isometric for their unique C*-norms; so $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are isometric on the union and extend to mutually inverse isomorphisms of the completions (for $p - q$ even, the completion of Theorem \claimref{tower.car-limit-even-charge}), carrying the closure of $B_{\infty}$ onto itself.

\emph{(ii).} If $n \ge 1$ then $x_{1} \notin B_{\infty}$, while for $n' = 0$ the plane algebra is the whole limit, so no pair isomorphism exists between $n \ge 1$ and $n' = 0$. For $n, n' \ge 1$: if the pairs are isomorphic, so are the relative commutants of $B_{\infty}$, which are $\Cl^{0}(p,q)$ and $\Cl^{0}(p',q')$ by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.plane-commutant-even-ground}(i); by its part (ii) these determine $n$ and the class $\{r, -r\} \bmod 8$. Conversely, (i) gives $(p,q) \to (q,p)$. For the shift $(p,q) \to (p-4, q+4)$ when $p \ge 4$: take four ground generators $x_{1}, \dots, x_{4}$ of square $+1$ and $\omega_{4} = x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}$, so $\omega_{4}^{2} = 1$, $\omega_{4}$ anticommutes with $x_{1}, \dots, x_{4}$ and commutes with every other generator. The elements $z_{i} = x_{i}\omega_{4}$ ($i \le 4$) satisfy $z_{i}^{2} = -1$, anticommute pairwise and with every other generator, and $z_{1}z_{2}z_{3}z_{4} = \omega_{4}$, so $x_{i} = z_{i}\omega_{4}$; together with the remaining ground generators and all plane generators, unchanged, they present $L_{p,q}$ as $L_{p-4,q+4}$ with $B_{\infty}$ fixed pointwise. The case $q \ge 4$ is the same with squares $-1$. For fixed $n$, $r = 2p - n$, so $r' \equiv r \pmod 8$ means $p' \equiv p \pmod 4$, reached by shifts within $0 \le p \le n$, and $r' \equiv -r$ means $p' \equiv n - p \pmod 4$, reached by one reversal followed by shifts.

\emph{(iii).} Over $\R$: for a blade $B$ and a generator $g$ (the blade argument of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.plane-commutant-even-ground}, Step 1): if $g \notin B$ then $gB = (-1)^{|B|}Bg$, which is supercommutation; if $g \in B$ then $gB = (-1)^{|B|-1}Bg$, which is not. Conjugation by $g$ acts diagonally on blades, so the supercommutant of all plane generators is spanned by the blades containing no plane generator, which span $\Cl(p,q)$. An isomorphism of graded pairs restricts to an isomorphism of these supercommutants, and $\Cl(p,q) \not\cong \Cl(q,p)$ for $r \not\equiv 0, 4 \pmod 8$ (the types for $r$ and $-r$ differ: $\R \oplus \R$ against $\C$, $\R$ against $\HH$, $\C$ against $\HH \oplus \HH$; Theorem \claimref{transport.classification-real-clifford-algebras}). For $\Phi\alpha\Phi^{-1}$, evaluate on the generators of $L_{q,p}$ through $\Psi$: $y_{i} = \Phi(x_{i})\Phi(e_{1}) \mapsto (-\Phi(x_{i}))(-\Phi(e_{1})) = y_{i}$; $e_{1} \mapsto -e_{1}$; $f_{j} = \Phi(e_{1})\Phi(e_{j+1}) \mapsto f_{j}$; $e_{j} = \Phi(e_{1})\Phi(f_{j-1}) \mapsto e_{j}$ for $j \ge 2$. So $\Phi\alpha\Phi^{-1}$ negates $e_{1}$ alone, which is $\operatorname{Ad}(e_{1}) \circ \alpha'$, and $e_{1}\alpha'(e_{1}) = -e_{1}^{2} = -1$. Its supercommutant of the planes is $\Phi(\Cl(p,q))$, generated by the $y_{i}e_{1}$. The blade argument holds verbatim after complexification, giving $\Cl(p,q)_{\C} \cong \Cl(p+q, 0)_{\C}$, which depends on $n$ alone; so over $\C$ the graded pair does not separate $r$ from $-r$ either.

\emph{(iv).} With $p - q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ the repairs have residues $r \pm 1$, both even; $r + 1 \equiv -(r - 1) \pmod 8$ would need $2r \equiv 0 \pmod 8$, impossible for $r$ odd. By (ii) the pairs are not isomorphic. Concretely the planes' commutant is $\Cl^{0}$ of the repair, whose centre is spanned by $1$ and the volume element $\omega$ with $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{r'/2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.plane-commutant-even-ground}, Step 3): $r' = r + 1 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ gives $\omega^{2} = -1$, a centre $\C$, and $r' = r - 1 \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ gives $\omega^{2} = 1$, a centre $\R \oplus \R$. The fused algebras themselves are isomorphic by Fact \claimref{rule2.imported-rule-2-matrix-units-forgotten}.

The check verifies (i) on truncations ($n \le 5$, two floors), including the inverse and the transported grading, the shift of (ii), and the centres of (iv), in exact arithmetic.

tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge.formal:
Let $p - q$ be even. The algebraic direct limit of the tower $(T_k, \iota_k)$ is canonically isomorphic to
\[
\varinjlim T_k \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}, \qquad \Mat_{2^\infty} := \varinjlim \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \ \ (m \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(m,m)),
\]
the ground algebra tensored with the algebraic $2^\infty$ matrix algebra. Equivalently, $\varinjlim T_k$ is the Clifford algebra of the infinite-dimensional quadratic space $\R^{p,q} \perp H_1 \perp H_2 \perp \cdots$.
tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge.technical:
For $p - q$ even, the algebraic direct limit of the tower $(T_k, \iota_k)$ is canonically $\varinjlim T_k \cong \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$, where $\Mat_{2^\infty} = \varinjlim \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ along $m \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(m,m)$. The proof transports the connecting maps to $\psi_k = \operatorname{Ad}(V_k) \circ \theta_k$, block doubling followed by conjugation, and removes the correctors stagewise with the invertible elements $W_{k+1} = \theta_k(W_k)\, V_k^{-1}$, so that the comparison squares commute exactly.

Equivalently, the limit is the Clifford algebra of the infinite-dimensional quadratic space $\R^{p,q} \perp H_1 \perp H_2 \perp \cdots$.
tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge.lay: Keep adding planes to the tower forever and take the union, purely algebraically. When the numbers of positive and negative directions differ by an even amount, the result has a clean description: the original algebra with entries in an infinite matrix algebra built by repeated doubling. Equivalently, it is the Clifford algebra of the infinite-dimensional space obtained by adding all the planes at once.
tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge.typing_note: Both edges are genuine premises; the second description rests on a general universal-property argument with no store reference.

proofs.main:
Write $A := \Cl(p,q)$, let $\varphi_k : T_k \to A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}$ be the isomorphisms of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, and transport the connecting maps: $\psi_k := \varphi_{k+1} \circ \iota_k \circ \varphi_k^{-1}$. By Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported},
\[
\psi_k \;=\; \Ad(V_k) \circ \theta_k, \qquad \theta_k(z) := z \otimes 1_{\,2 \times 2}\ \text{(block doubling)},
\]
with $V_k$ the split corrector displayed there. The comparison system is $(A \otimes \Mat_{2^k},\, \theta_k)$, whose limit is $A \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$ by definition. Intertwine the two systems stagewise: set $W_0 := 1$ and recursively $W_{k+1} := \theta_k(W_k)\, V_k^{-1}$, each $W_k$ an invertible element of $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}$, and define $\lambda_k := \Ad(W_k)$. Then
\[
\lambda_{k+1} \circ \psi_k = \Ad(W_{k+1}) \circ \Ad(V_k) \circ \theta_k = \Ad(\theta_k(W_k)) \circ \theta_k = \theta_k \circ \Ad(W_k) = \theta_k \circ \lambda_k ,
\]
using $\theta_k \circ \Ad(W_k) = \Ad(\theta_k(W_k)) \circ \theta_k$ (a unital homomorphism carries conjugation to conjugation by the image). The squares commute exactly, so the $\lambda_k$ assemble into an isomorphism of the direct limits: $\varinjlim T_k \cong A \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$.

For the second description: the algebraic direct limit of Clifford algebras of a nested chain of quadratic spaces along the induced embeddings is the Clifford algebra of the union (both sides satisfy the same universal property for the union space, and every element of either side lies at a finite stage). Canonicity: the $\varphi_k$ and the correcting elements $W_k$ are built from the ordered planes and volume elements only.

tower.answers-iteration-question.formal:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration in the sense of \cite[Hyp.~2.1]{ButlerT4}, with trivial radical line bundle and compact wall as in Fact \claimref{tower.wall-package}, presenting the transport demand of the series' geometric setting.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Where ascent is forced.} On the physical closure, one ascent completes the description: by Fact \claimref{tower.wall-package} the one-sided completion is nondegenerate up to and including the wall and the transported reciprocal divides totally there; nothing on the physical side demands a second rung. Beyond the physical region, the demand repeats: by Fact \claimref{tower.wall-package} the degeneration relocates to a tame shadow wall, and the infinite wall sequence carries exactly one rung of this paper's tower per wall, displaced successively away from the physical region.
\item \emph{Why the clock never ticks.} Theorem \claimref{tower.rigidity-clock-frozen}: the tower is Morita-stationary from its first step, and the mod-8 structure classifies the eight parallel towers, not stages of one.
\item \emph{What the limit is.} Theorems \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge} and \claimref{tower.car-limit-even-charge}: for even transport charge, the ground algebra tensored with the free fermionic field algebra, the modes being the transported null pairs themselves.
\end{enumerate}
The depth of the hierarchy, on this account: one forced conformal ascent, plus a fermionic ladder of capacity, one qubit per rung.
tower.answers-iteration-question.technical:
Assuming tameness, for a corank-one degeneration with trivial radical line bundle and compact wall, the iteration question has three answers. On the physical closure one ascent suffices: the one-sided completion is nondegenerate up to and including the wall and the transported reciprocal divides totally there. Beyond the physical region the degeneration relocates to tame shadow walls, and the infinite wall sequence carries one rung of the tower per wall, displaced successively away from the physical region.

The clock never ticks, because the tower is Morita-stationary from its first step and the mod-8 structure classifies eight parallel towers rather than stages of one. For even transport charge the limit is the ground algebra tensored with the free fermionic field algebra, the modes being the transported null pairs. The depth of the hierarchy is thus one forced conformal ascent plus a fermionic ladder of capacity, one qubit per rung.
tower.answers-iteration-question.lay: The question was how many times the series' completion step has to be repeated. Under the tameness premise, and for a compact wall with a trivial radical line, on the physical side of a degeneration the answer is once; further steps are demanded only beyond it, one for each successive hidden wall. Repeating the step never changes the algebra's essential type, and in the infinite limit, for even charge, it simply adds the modes of a free fermion field, one qubit per step.

tower.car-limit-even-charge.formal:
Continue with $p - q$ even. Complexifying and completing in the unique C*-norm of the complexified limit (Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}): the result is
\[
\Cl(p,q)_\C \,\otimes\, \CAR,
\]
where $\CAR$ is the CAR algebra of countably many fermionic modes, the unique Glimm UHF algebra of type $2^\infty$; the mode operators are represented by the adjoined null vectors themselves via Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}, with $w_j = v_j^*$ both for the intrinsic *-structure of Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} and for the Fock inner product. The completed tower is the ground algebra tensored with the algebra of a free fermionic quantum field: iterated transport is second quantisation, one mode per rung.
tower.car-limit-even-charge.technical:
For $p - q$ even, complexify the algebraic limit of the tower and complete it in its unique C*-norm. The complexification is that of the $*$-structure lemma: $\C$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ in a tensor factor, with unit $1 \otimes I_4$ central and in no floor; for the physical ground it is not the ground's own volume element $\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, which anticommutes with the ground vectors. The result is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$, where $\CAR$ is the CAR algebra of countably many fermionic modes, the unique UHF algebra of type $2^\infty$.

The mode operators are the adjoined null vectors themselves, $a_j = w_j$ and $a_j^\dagger = v_j$, and $w_j = v_j^*$ holds both for the intrinsic *-structure of the tower and for the Fock inner product. The completed tower is thus the ground algebra tensored with the algebra of a free fermionic field: iterated transport is second quantisation, one mode per rung.
tower.car-limit-even-charge.lay: Repeatedly applying the transport step builds an infinite tower of algebras. When the signature difference is even and the tower is completed, it becomes the original algebra combined with the standard algebra of a free field of fermions with countably many modes. Each rung of the tower contributes exactly one fermionic mode, and the null vectors added at that rung act directly as its creation and annihilation operators.
tower.car-limit-even-charge.typing_note: All five extracted edges are cited in the proof as premises; no context references to assess.

proofs.main:
Complexification commutes with direct limits and with tensor products, so by Theorem \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge} the complexified limit is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}^\C$, with $\Mat_{2^\infty}^\C$ the algebraic $2^\infty$ matrix algebra over $\C$: an increasing union of full matrix algebras, and the identification is a *-isomorphism because the correctors $W_k$ are unitary (Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}). By Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms} each stage is a C*-algebra with its unique C*-norm, the connecting maps are isometric, and the union carries a unique C*-norm; its completion is Glimm's UHF algebra of type $2^\infty$ tensored with the finite-dimensional factor $\Cl(p,q)_\C$, by Fact \claimref{tower.glimms-classification-car-uniqueness}(i), the tensor factor changing nothing (finite-dimensional algebras are nuclear, and the tensor product of the completions is the completion of the algebraic tensor product).

The identification with the CAR algebra is effected by the tower's own generators rather than by a Jordan-Wigner transformation. The elements $a_j := w_j$ (annihilation) and $a_j^\dagger := v_j$ (creation) of the limit satisfy the CAR exactly (Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}), and $a_j^\dagger = a_j^*$ for the intrinsic *-structure, since $v_j^* = w_j$ (Lemma \claimref{tower.structure-tower-c-norms}). The Fock module of Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}, taken over all $k$, is $\Lambda^\bullet W_\infty$ with the inner product making the wedge monomials in the $v_j$ orthonormal, and its vacuum is annihilated by every $a_j$. In it, wedge and contraction are mutually adjoint: for ordered monomials $v_S$ and $v_T$, both $\langle v_j \wedge v_S,\, v_T \rangle$ and $\langle v_S,\, \iota_{\varphi_j} v_T \rangle$ vanish unless $j \notin S$ and $T = \{j\} \cup S$, in which case both equal the sign that moves $v_j$ to its ordered position; linearity does the rest. So the *-relations are implemented by the adjoint for this inner product, and the generated C*-algebra is a representation of the CAR over the mode space $\ell^2$. By Fact \claimref{tower.glimms-classification-car-uniqueness}(ii), the C*-subalgebra generated by the $a_j, a_j^\dagger$ in the completion is \emph{the} CAR algebra; it is the completed image of the plane factor $\Mat_{2^\infty}^\C$ (the $j$-th plane's complexified algebra is generated by its pair), and the ground factor commutes with it. So the completion is $\Cl(p,q)_\C \otimes \CAR$, with the mode operators the transported null vectors themselves.

tower.commuting-copies.formal:
Inside $T_k$, let $B_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the $2k$ plane generators $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$, and let $A_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the twisted base generators $x^{(k)} := x\,\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots \omega_k$ for $x$ among the ground generators. Then: $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$; $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$ via $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$ (the twisted generators satisfy the ground Clifford relations); $A_k$ and $B_k$ commute elementwise; and multiplication $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ is an isomorphism of algebras,
\[
\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \;=\; \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q)).
\]
The isomorphism is canonical given the ordered planes, and compatible with the tower embeddings up to the twist tracked in the section “The CAR limit”.
tower.commuting-copies.technical:
Inside the floor $T_k$, the $2k$ plane generators generate a subalgebra $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, and the twisted ground generators $x^{(k)} = x\,\omega_1 \cdots \omega_k$ generate a subalgebra $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$, because the twist preserves the ground Clifford relations. The two subalgebras commute elementwise, and multiplication is an algebra isomorphism $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$, giving $\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \cong \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) = \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$.

The isomorphism is canonical once the planes are ordered, and is compatible with the tower embeddings up to the grade twist tracked in the limit construction.
tower.commuting-copies.lay: Adding hyperbolic planes to a Clifford algebra creates nothing essentially new. The enlarged algebra splits into two pieces that commute with each other: a slightly twisted copy of the original algebra, and an algebra of ordinary real square matrices. So each floor of the tower is the ground algebra with matrix entries.
tower.commuting-copies.typing_note: All three edges are used; the edge to the grade-twist lemma supports only the final compatibility clause, which the proof defers to that lemma.

proofs.main:
\emph{$B_k \cong \Cl(k,k)$.} The $2k$ generators are orthonormal for the split form ($e_j^2 = 1$, $f_j^2 = -1$, pairwise orthogonal), so the universal property (\claimref{std-algebra.existence-uniqueness}) gives a surjection $\Cl(k,k) \to B_k$; it is injective because the $2^{2k}$ blades in the letters $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$ are part of the blade basis of $T_k$ (\claimref{std-algebra.blade-basis}), hence independent. \emph{$\Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$} by induction using the series' own results: $\Cl(0,0) = \R$, and $\Cl(j{+}1,j{+}1) \cong \Mat_2(\Cl(j,j))$ is Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} with base $\Cl(j,j)$, the $(j{+}1)$-st plane carrying the outer index, so $\Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_2(\Mat_2(\cdots)) = \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$.

\emph{$A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$.} By Lemma \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes}, $\Omega_k$ commutes with ground generators and $\Omega_k^2 = 1$, so for ground generators $x, y$:
\[
x^{(k)} y^{(k)} + y^{(k)} x^{(k)} = x \Omega_k y \Omega_k + y \Omega_k x \Omega_k = (xy + yx)\,\Omega_k^2 = 2B(x,y) .
\]
The universal property gives an algebra map $\Cl(p,q) \to A_k$, $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$; it sends the base blade $x_I$ to $x_I\,\Omega_k^{|I| \bmod 2}$, and these images are distinct nonzero blades (times a fixed invertible even element), hence independent: the map is an isomorphism onto $A_k$.

\emph{Commutation.} For a ground generator $x$ and any plane generator $g \in \{e_j, f_j\}$: $x$ anticommutes with $g$, and $\Omega_k$ anticommutes with $g$ (Lemma \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes}), so $x^{(k)} g = x \Omega_k g = -x g \Omega_k = g x \Omega_k = g x^{(k)}$. Generators commute, hence the subalgebras do.

\emph{Multiplication is an isomorphism.} Commutation makes $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ an algebra map. It is surjective: its image contains every plane generator, contains $\Omega_k \in B_k$, and therefore contains each ground generator $x = x^{(k)} \Omega_k$. Source and target both have dimension $2^n \cdot 2^{2k} = 2^{n + 2k}$, so a surjective linear map is an isomorphism. Finally $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) = \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$. Canonicity: the construction used only the ordered orthogonal planes and their volume elements, no basis choices in the ground algebra. The compatibility with $\iota_k$ is Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner} below: under these identifications $\iota_k$ is the twisted diagonal, the twist being conjugation by $\Omega$-data that the section “The CAR limit” tracks.

tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-tran.formal:
Let $p - q$ be even, $A := \Cl(p,q)$, and let $\varphi_k : T_k \to A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ be the identifications of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, with every plane's matrix units labelled as in Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} and the planes nested in order, the $(k{+}1)$-st plane carrying the outer index of $\Mat_{2^{k+1}} = \Mat_2(\Mat_{2^k})$. Write $\theta_k(z) := z \otimes 1_{2 \times 2}$ for block doubling in the outer index, $u_A \in A$ for the ground volume element, and $\overline\Omega_k \in \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ for the image of $\Omega_k = \omega_1 \cdots \omega_k$. Then the transported connecting map $\psi_k := \varphi_{k+1} \circ \iota_k \circ \varphi_k^{-1}$ is
\[
\psi_k \;=\; \Ad(V_k) \circ \theta_k, \qquad
V_k \;:=\; \begin{pmatrix} u_A \otimes 1_{2^k} & 0 \\ 0 & 1_A \otimes \overline\Omega_k \end{pmatrix},
\]
with $V_k$ invertible ($u_A^2 = \pm 1$, $\Omega_k^2 = 1$). In this labelling and for $n = p + q \ge 1$, the corrector is \emph{not} the transported single-step corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_k})$ of Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner}: transporting through $\varphi$ splits the correction across the two tensor legs, the ground volume acting in the first corner and the planes' volume in the second. The labelling convention of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} matters: with $vw$ and $wv$ exchanged for the new plane, the transported single-step corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_k})$ is the one that works and $V_k$ is not; for $n = 0$ the two coincide.
tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-tran.technical:
Take $p - q$ even and $A = \Cl(p,q)$, and identify each floor with $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ by the commuting-copies isomorphisms $\varphi_k$, with the planes nested in order and the newest plane carrying the outer matrix index. The tower embedding then becomes $\psi_k = \varphi_{k+1} \circ \iota_k \circ \varphi_k^{-1} = \operatorname{Ad}(V_k) \circ \theta_k$, where $\theta_k(z) = z \otimes 1_{2 \times 2}$ is block doubling and $V_k = \operatorname{diag}(u_A \otimes 1_{2^k},\ 1_A \otimes \overline\Omega_k)$ is invertible, $u_A$ being the ground volume element and $\overline\Omega_k$ the image of the planes' volume element.

In this labelling, and for $n = p + q \ge 1$, the corrector is not the transported single-step corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_k})$: transport splits the correction across the two tensor legs, the ground volume acting in the first corner and the planes' volume in the second. The labelling convention for the matrix units matters: with $vw$ and $wv$ exchanged for the new plane, the transported single-step corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_k})$ is the one that works and $V_k$ is not; for $n = 0$ the two coincide. The proof checks both sides on generators.
tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-tran.lay: When each floor of the tower is rewritten as matrices over the ground algebra, the map from one floor to the next becomes simple block doubling followed by a conjugation. This result writes down the conjugating element exactly. It has two pieces sitting in the two diagonal corners, one built from the ground algebra's volume element and one from that of the added planes, rather than the single correction a one-step view would suggest (with the matrix units labelled as the store fixes them; with the other labelling the single correction is the right one).
tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-tran.typing_note: Added commuting-copies, whose identifications varphi_k the statement is built on and the proof uses (x^(k) maps to x tensor 1); the three extracted edges are all used in the generator checks.

proofs.main:
Both sides are unital algebra maps into $A \otimes \Mat_{2^{k+1}}$, so it suffices to check them on generators of $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}$: the elements $x \otimes 1$ for ground generators $x$, and $1 \otimes b$ for $b$ the image of a plane generator $g \in \{e_j, f_j\}$, $j \leq k$.

\emph{Ground generators.} $\varphi_k^{-1}(x \otimes 1) = x^{(k)} = x\,\Omega_k$ (the twisted generator of \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}). In $T_{k+1}$, $\Omega_{k+1} = \Omega_k\, \omega_{k+1}$ and $\omega_{k+1}^2 = 1$ give $x^{(k)} = x^{(k+1)}\, \omega_{k+1}$. Under $\varphi_{k+1}$, $x^{(k+1)} \mapsto x \otimes 1_{2^{k+1}}$ by definition, and $\omega_{k+1} \mapsto 1_A \otimes \operatorname{diag}(-1_{2^k}, +1_{2^k})$ by Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} for the outer plane. Hence
\[
\psi_k(x \otimes 1) \;=\; x \otimes \operatorname{diag}(-1_{2^k},\, +1_{2^k}).
\]
On the other side, $\theta_k(x \otimes 1) = x \otimes 1_{2^{k+1}}$, and conjugating cornerwise by $V_k$: the first corner gives $(u_A \otimes 1)(x \otimes 1)(u_A \otimes 1)^{-1} = u_A x u_A^{-1} \otimes 1 = -x \otimes 1$ (Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner}, $n$ even), the second gives $(1 \otimes \overline\Omega_k)(x \otimes 1)(1 \otimes \overline\Omega_k)^{-1} = x \otimes 1$. The two sides agree.

\emph{Plane generators.} $\varphi_k^{-1}(1 \otimes b) = g$ and $\iota_k(g) = g \in B_{k+1}$. The nesting embeds $B_k$ into $\Mat_2(B_k)$ as the twisted diagonal of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} with base $B_k = \Cl(k,k)$: $g \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(g, \hat g)$, with $\hat{\cdot}$ the grade involution of $B_k$, which by Lemma \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes} is implemented by $\Omega_k$ (it anticommutes with every plane generator and squares to one). Under $\varphi_{k+1}$ this reads
\[
\psi_k(1 \otimes b) \;=\; 1 \otimes \operatorname{diag}\bigl(b,\ \overline\Omega_k\, b\, \overline\Omega_k^{-1}\bigr),
\]
and conjugating $\theta_k(1 \otimes b) = 1 \otimes \operatorname{diag}(b, b)$ cornerwise by $V_k$ gives exactly the same: the first corner commutes with $u_A \otimes 1$, the second is conjugated by $\overline\Omega_k$. The two sides agree.

Two unital algebra maps agreeing on a generating set agree, and $V_k$ is invertible as stated. One full stage of this identity, with the corrector exactly as displayed, is verified in exact arithmetic over the ground algebra $\Cl(1,1)$ in the script (the section “Machine verification”).

tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung.formal: Let $W_k := \operatorname{span}\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, a maximal isotropic subspace of $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$. The Chevalley action ($v_j$ by wedge, $w_j$ by contraction against the pairing) makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$, of dimension $2^k$, an irreducible module over $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, with the vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ annihilated by every $w_j$ and cyclic for the $v_j$. Each rung doubles the module: $\Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1}$, one qubit per rung.
tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung.technical:
Let $W_k = \operatorname{span}\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, a maximal isotropic subspace of $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$. The Chevalley action, with each $v_j$ acting by wedge product and each $w_j$ by contraction against the pairing, makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$, of dimension $2^k$, an irreducible module over $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$. The vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ is annihilated by every $w_j$ and is cyclic for the $v_j$.

Each rung doubles the module, $\Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1}$: one qubit per rung.
tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung.lay: The planes added in the tower act naturally on a space built like the state space of fermions: an empty vacuum state, with raising operators that fill slots and lowering operators that empty them. Nothing smaller carries this action, and after k planes the space has dimension 2 to the power k. Each new plane doubles it, adding one qubit per rung of the tower.
tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung.typing_note: Both edges are genuine premises: isotropy of W_k from the ladder-pair proposition, and simplicity of B_k from commuting copies.

proofs.main:
\emph{The action.} $W_k$ is isotropic (Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) of dimension $k$, maximal since the split form $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$ has Witt index $k$ (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-decomposition}). Define, for $\xi \in \Lambda^\bullet W_k$,
\[
c(v_j)\,\xi = v_j \wedge \xi, \qquad c(w_j)\,\xi = \iota_{\varphi_j}\,\xi, \qquad \varphi_j := 2\langle w_j, \cdot\,\rangle|_{W_k} \in W_k^* ,
\]
so $\varphi_j(v_i) = \delta_{ij}$, and extend linearly to arbitrary vectors $\alpha = \sum_j (a_j v_j + b_j w_j)$.

\emph{The three anticommutator families,} elementary and proved outright. Wedge operators square to zero and pairwise anticommute, since $v \wedge v' = -v' \wedge v$ and $v \wedge v = 0$. The contraction $\iota_\varphi$ acts on monomials by
\[
\iota_\varphi(u_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge u_s) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{s} (-1)^{i-1}\, \varphi(u_i)\; u_1 \wedge \cdots \widehat{u_i} \cdots \wedge u_s .
\]
Two contractions anticommute: in $\iota_\varphi \iota_\psi + \iota_\psi \iota_\varphi$ applied to a monomial, the term deleting $u_j$ then $u_i$ (with $i < j$) in the first composite carries the sign
\[
(-1)^{j-1}(-1)^{i-1},
\qquad \text{against} \qquad
(-1)^{i-1}(-1)^{j-2}
\]
for the matching term of the second composite, which deletes $u_i$ then $u_j$; the shift by one arises because removing $u_i$ first moves $u_j$ up a slot, and the opposite signs cancel the terms pairwise. The mixed anticommutator: the displayed expansion gives $\iota_\varphi(v \wedge \xi) = \varphi(v)\,\xi - v \wedge \iota_\varphi(\xi)$ (the $i = 1$ term, then the rest), so $\{v \wedge \cdot\,,\, \iota_\varphi\} = \varphi(v)\,\mathrm{id}$.

\emph{The Clifford relation, and the isomorphism.} Combining the three families,
\[
c(\alpha)^2 = \Bigl(\sum_j b_j \varphi_j\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_i a_i v_i\Bigr)\,\mathrm{id} = \sum_j a_j b_j\,\mathrm{id} = Q(\alpha)\,\mathrm{id},
\]
since $Q(\alpha) = \sum_j 2 a_j b_j \langle v_j, w_j\rangle = \sum_j a_j b_j$. By the universal property (\claimref{std-algebra.existence-uniqueness}) $c$ extends to an algebra map $B_k \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W_k)$. It is unital and nonzero with simple source ($B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}), hence injective; source and target both have dimension $2^{2k} = (2^k)^2$, so it is an isomorphism, and the module is irreducible.

\emph{Vacuum, cyclicity, doubling.} The vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ is sent to zero by every contraction and generates everything under wedges: $v_{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge v_{i_r} = c(v_{i_1}) \cdots c(v_{i_r})\,1$. The doubling statement is the exterior algebra of a direct sum.

tower.glimms-classification-car-uniquene.formal: (i) The completion of an increasing union of full matrix algebras $\Mat_{2^k}(\C)$ along unital embeddings, in its unique C*-norm, is the UHF algebra of type $2^\infty$, unique up to *-isomorphism. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Glimm1960}. (ii) Any two C*-algebras generated by elements satisfying the canonical anticommutation relations over a given complex mode space, with $*$ matching the pairing, are canonically *-isomorphic; the CAR algebra over $\ell^2$ is *-isomorphic to the $2^\infty$ UHF algebra. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~5.2.5]{BratteliRobinson1997}.
tower.glimms-classification-car-uniquene.technical:
(i) Completing an increasing union of full matrix algebras $\Mat_{2^k}(\C)$ along unital embeddings, in its unique C*-norm, gives the UHF algebra of type $2^\infty$, unique up to *-isomorphism (Glimm).

(ii) Any two C*-algebras generated by elements satisfying the canonical anticommutation relations over the same complex mode space, with $*$ matching the pairing, are canonically *-isomorphic, and the CAR algebra over $\ell^2$ is *-isomorphic to the $2^\infty$ UHF algebra (Bratteli and Robinson).
tower.glimms-classification-car-uniquene.lay: Gluing together ever larger matrix algebras, doubling in size each time, and completing gives one specific infinite-dimensional algebra, whatever unital gluing maps are used. Separately, the algebra generated by fermion creation and annihilation operators is determined by their relations alone, and for countably many modes it is that same algebra. Both are standard results imported from the operator-algebra literature.

tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner.formal: Under the isomorphism of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, the tower embedding $\iota_k$ becomes the twisted diagonal $a \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$ of \cite[Thm.~7.1]{ButlerT1} (in the corner identification of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}; in the twisted coordinates with $E_{11} = vw$ it reads $\operatorname{diag}(\hat a, a)$). If $p - q$ is even, $\Cl(p,q)$ is central simple over $\R$, the grade involution is an $\R$-algebra automorphism fixing the centre, and it is inner, implemented by the ground volume element $u$ (which anticommutes with vectors precisely when $n$ is even): $\hat a = u a u^{-1}$. Consequently $\operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a) = U \operatorname{diag}(a, a)\, U^{-1}$ with $U = \operatorname{diag}(1, u)$: the twist conjugates away at the level of the single step. (How the correction transports through the identifications of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, which is what the limit theorem needs, is Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported}; the stagewise corrector is \emph{not} simply this $U$.) If $p - q$ is odd the grade involution acts nontrivially on the centre ($\R \oplus \R$ or $\C$) and is outer; no inner correction exists.
tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner.technical:
Under the commuting-copies isomorphism, the tower embedding $\iota_k$ is the twisted diagonal $a \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$ (in the corner identification of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}; in the twisted coordinates with $E_{11} = vw$ it reads $\operatorname{diag}(\hat a, a)$), with $\hat a$ the grade involution. When $p - q$ is even, $\Cl(p,q)$ is central simple over $\R$ and the grade involution is inner: it is conjugation by the ground volume element $u$, which then anticommutes with every vector, so $\hat a = u a u^{-1}$. Hence $\operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a) = U \operatorname{diag}(a, a)\, U^{-1}$ with $U = \operatorname{diag}(1, u)$, and the twist conjugates away at a single step.

This single-step corrector is not the stagewise corrector the limit needs, which is handled by a separate compatibility lemma. When $p - q$ is odd, the centre is $\R \oplus \R$ or $\C$, the grade involution acts nontrivially on it, and so it is outer: no inner correction exists.
tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner.lay: Each step up the tower places the previous algebra inside the next one with a small twist, built from the operation that flips the sign of every vector. When the numbers of positive and negative directions differ by an even amount, the twist is only a change of viewpoint at each step: conjugating by a single element, the volume element of the ground algebra, undoes it. When they differ by an odd amount, the twist moves the centre of the algebra and cannot be undone in this way.

proofs.main:
The matrix form of $\iota_k$ is Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} applied with base $T_k$: the new plane's ladder pair supplies the matrix units, and the base embeds as $a \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$, the grade involution taken in $T_k$. Note the parity is stable: $\dim$ of floor $k$ is $n + 2k$, of the same parity as $n$, so ``even charge'' is a property of the whole tower.

Even charge: $n$ even makes $\Cl(p,q)$ (and every floor) central simple over $\R$ (its centre is $\R$, \claimref{primer.centre}) \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001}. The grade involution is an $\R$-algebra automorphism fixing the centre $\R$ pointwise, so its innerness is an instance of the Skolem-Noether theorem \cite{Pierce1982}; nothing need be imported, because the implementing element is exhibited directly: the volume element $u = x_1 \cdots x_n$ of an orthogonal generator frame satisfies $u x = (-1)^{n-1} x u = -xu$ for each generator $x$ (\claimref{std-algebra.pseudoscalar-commutation}) (move $x$ through $n$ letters, one coincidence), and $u^2 = \pm 1$ is invertible; so $\Ad_u(x) = u x u^{-1} = -x = \hat x$ on generators, and two automorphisms agreeing on generators agree. The displayed conjugation is then the block computation $U \operatorname{diag}(a,a)\, U^{-1} = \operatorname{diag}(a, u a u^{-1})$ with $U = \operatorname{diag}(1, u)$, invertible in $\Mat_2(T_k)$.

Odd charge: the centre of each floor is $\R \oplus \R$ ($d \equiv 1 \bmod 4$) or $\C$ ($d \equiv 3 \bmod 4$), generated by $1$ and the volume element $\omega$, which is odd (its length $n + 2k$ is odd) and is therefore sent by the grade involution to $-\omega$: the involution exchanges the two central idempotents $\tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$, respectively conjugates the central complex structure. An inner automorphism fixes the centre pointwise; the grade involution does not, so it is outer, and no unitary correction of the diagonal exists.

tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors.formal:
In $T_k$, the adjoined null pairs satisfy, exactly and at the level of vectors,
\[
v_i v_j + v_j v_i = 0, \qquad w_i w_j + w_j w_i = 0, \qquad v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij}\,,
\]
for all $1 \leq i, j \leq k$: a system of $k$ fermionic modes, with no normal-ordering, no completion, and no representation chosen. Adding a rung adds one mode and touches none of the existing relations.
tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors.technical:
In the $k$-th algebra of the tower, $T_k = \Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k)$, each adjoined hyperbolic plane carries a normalised null pair $(v_i, w_i)$. These vectors satisfy $v_i v_j + v_j v_i = 0$, $w_i w_j + w_j w_i = 0$ and $v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij}$ for all $1 \leq i, j \leq k$, which are the canonical anticommutation relations of $k$ fermionic modes. The relations hold exactly, among vectors of the algebra, with no normal ordering, no completion and no choice of representation.

Each relation is an instance of the Clifford relation $ab + ba = 2\langle a, b\rangle$ for vectors: the null vectors have $Q(v_i) = Q(w_i) = 0$, distinct planes are orthogonal, and the hyperbolic normalisation gives $\langle v_i, w_i\rangle = \tfrac12$. The vectors of a new rung are orthogonal to all earlier generators, so adding a rung adds one mode and leaves the existing relations untouched.
tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors.lay: Each step up the tower adds a new pair of special zero-length directions to the space. Taken together, these pairs obey exactly the algebraic rules that quantum theory uses for fermionic modes, the kind of states occupied by particles such as electrons, with one mode per step. The rules hold for the directions themselves, so nothing has to be added or chosen to make them work, and a new step never disturbs the modes already present.
tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors.typing_note: no claim edges, the proof uses only the Clifford relation on vectors and the construction of the tower; obj.tower.tower would fit in about but was not added

proofs.main: Every displayed relation is an instance of the single Clifford relation $\alpha\beta + \beta\alpha = 2\langle\alpha, \beta\rangle$ on vectors (\claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}), as for any Witt basis (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}): the $v$'s are pairwise orthogonal null vectors ($\langle v_i, v_j \rangle = 0$ for $i \neq j$ since the planes are orthogonal, and $v_i^2 = 0$ since $v_i$ is null), likewise the $w$'s, and $\langle v_i, w_j \rangle = \tfrac12\delta_{ij}$ by the hyperbolic normalisation within each plane and orthogonality across planes. A new rung's vectors are orthogonal to all previous generators, so the old relations are untouched.

tower.rigidity-clock-frozen.formal: Along the tower: the transport charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$ is constant; the division-ring type, simplicity class, and centre of every floor equal those of the ground floor; every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor; and the obstruction taxonomy of \cite{ButlerT1} is floor-independent: in particular a type-C obstruction (a central idempotent) never arises by transport from a simple ground algebra, at any height. The physical tower is $\Cl(1{+}k, 3{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^{k+1}}(\HH)$, frozen at clock position $6$. Bott periodicity manifests as immediate freeze, not eventual return.
tower.rigidity-clock-frozen.technical:
Along the tower the transport charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$ is constant, since $(p{+}k) - (q{+}k) = p - q$. Each floor is a matrix algebra over the ground floor, so its division-ring type, simplicity class and centre equal those of the ground floor, and it is Morita equivalent to the ground floor. The obstruction taxonomy is therefore floor-independent; in particular a type-C obstruction, a central idempotent, never arises by transport from a simple ground algebra, at any height.

For the physical tower, $\Cl(1{+}k, 3{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^{k+1}}(\HH)$ sits at clock position $6$ for every $k$: Bott periodicity shows up as immediate freeze, not eventual return.
tower.rigidity-clock-frozen.lay: Building the tower by adding pairs of opposite-signed directions never changes the essential type of the algebra. Every floor has the same underlying number system, the same centre and the same kinds of obstruction as the ground floor. For the spacetime algebra, every floor is a matrix algebra over the quaternions, so the eight-step Bott clock does not advance along the tower: it stays where it starts.
tower.rigidity-clock-frozen.typing_note: All four edges are genuine premises of the proof, including the imported Morita fact.

proofs.main: The charge is $(p{+}k) - (q{+}k) = p - q$, constant. All structural claims then follow from Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} and Lemma \claimref{tower.matrix-amplification-structural-properties}: centres agree by (i); if $A \cong \Mat_r(D)$ then $\Mat_{2^k}(A) \cong \Mat_{2^k r}(D)$ by (iii), the same division ring; simplicity propagates by (ii), and the block structure of a semisimple ground floor by (iv); and every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor by Fact \claimref{tower.morita-equivalence-algebra-amplification}. The taxonomy statement: by Fact \claimref{transport.existence-classification-type-c}, type C occurs exactly when the centre is $\R \oplus \R$; the centre is floor-independent by Lemma \claimref{tower.matrix-amplification-structural-properties}(i), so a simple ground floor (centre $\R$ or $\C$) propagates: no floor of its tower ever hosts a type-C obstruction. For the physical case, $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ \cite{Porteous1995} (\claimref{std-algebra.sta-matrix}), so floor $k$ is $\Mat_{2^k}(\Mat_2(\HH)) = \Mat_{2^{k+1}}(\HH)$, and $1 - 3 \equiv 6 \pmod 8$.

tower.structure-tower-c-norms.formal: Fix the tower's frames: an orthogonal ground frame $x_1, \dots, x_n$ diagonalising $Q$, and the plane frames $e_j, f_j$. Each complexified floor is $T_k^{\,\C} = T_k \otimes_\R \C$ with $\C$ read as $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ in the second factor (conventions, the unit principle, U1): its unit $1 \otimes I_4$ commutes with every ground and plane generator by construction and is not an element of the floor (the odd extensions of U3 are floor by floor and exist only for even $m$); for the physical ground $\Cl(1,3)$ it is a unit of the scalar factor, not the ground volume element $u_A = \gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, which lies in the floor and anticommutes with the ground generators, and the two are not identified; complex matrices are read with entries in the same field. On each complexified floor $T_k^{\,\C}$ there is a unique conjugate-linear antiautomorphism $*$ with $x^* = x$ for every frame generator with $x^2 = 1$ and $x^* = -x$ for every frame generator with $x^2 = -1$. Under it: every frame generator, every blade in the frame, and every ground or plane volume element is unitary ($z^* z = 1$); the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_j^* = w_j$; the connecting maps $\iota_k$, the identifications $\varphi_k$ of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, the block doublings $\theta_k$, and the correctors $V_k$ and $W_k$ of Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported} and Theorem \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge} are all compatible with $*$ (the maps are *-homomorphisms, the correctors unitary). If moreover $p - q$ is even, each $T_k^{\,\C}$ is *-isomorphic to $\Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$, $m := n + 2k$, with $*$ the conjugate transpose; consequently each floor carries a unique C*-norm, every unital *-monomorphism between floors is isometric, and the increasing union $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ carries a unique C*-norm.
tower.structure-tower-c-norms.technical:
On each complexified floor $T_k^{\,\C}$ of the tower, with frame generators fixed, there is a unique conjugate-linear antiautomorphism $*$ fixing every frame generator with $Q(x) = 1$ and negating every frame generator with $Q(x) = -1$. Under it every frame generator, frame blade and ground or plane volume element is unitary, $z^* z = 1$; the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_j^* = w_j$; the connecting maps $\iota_k$, the identifications $\varphi_k$ and the block doublings $\theta_k$ are *-homomorphisms; and the correctors $V_k$, $W_k$ are unitary.

If moreover $p - q$ is even, a tensor-Pauli representation identifies $T_k^{\,\C}$ with $\Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$, $m = n + 2k$, carrying $*$ to the conjugate transpose. Consequently each floor has a unique C*-norm, every unital *-monomorphism between floors is isometric, and the increasing union $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ carries a unique C*-norm.
tower.structure-tower-c-norms.lay: Once complex numbers are allowed, each level of the tower of algebras carries a natural notion of adjoint, fixed by how it acts on the basic generators, and every map used to build the tower respects it. When the signature difference is even, every level is an ordinary algebra of complex square matrices. Such an algebra has exactly one way of measuring size that is compatible with the adjoint, and so does the union of all the levels.
tower.structure-tower-c-norms.typing_note: The statement asserts *-compatibility of the maps and correctors constructed in the three context results and the proof checks it from their explicit form, so they were added as premises; the rule-1 matrix units are also used directly. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main:
\emph{Existence and uniqueness.} Renormalise the $m$ frame generators of floor $k$ to $y_i := x_i$ when $x_i^2 = 1$ and $y_i := x_i \otimes I_4$ when $x_i^2 = -1$ ($1 \otimes I_4$ the scalar of the complexification), so that $y_i^2 = 1$ and the $y_i$ pairwise anticommute. Reversal, the unique real antiautomorphism of a Clifford algebra fixing its generating vectors (the universal property applied to the opposite algebra; \claimref{std-algebra.involution-properties}), extends conjugate-linearly to $T_k^{\,\C}$; call the extension $*$. It is conjugate-linear and antimultiplicative by construction, fixes each $y_i$, and on the original generators unwinds to exactly the displayed values: for $x^2 = -1$, $x = -y\,(1 \otimes I_4)$ gives $x^* = (1 \otimes \overline{-I_4})\,y^* = (1 \otimes I_4)\,y = -x$. Uniqueness holds because a conjugate-linear antiautomorphism is determined by its values on the generators.

\emph{Unitarity and adjoint pairs.} $y_i^* y_i = y_i^2 = 1$, and each original generator satisfies $x^* x = 1$ in both cases ($x^2 = 1$ gives $x^*x = x^2 = 1$; $x^2 = -1$ gives $x^*x = -x^2 = 1$). A product of unitaries is unitary by telescoping, $(z_1 \cdots z_s)^* (z_1 \cdots z_s) = z_s^* \cdots z_1^* z_1 \cdots z_s = 1$; blades, the ground volume $u_A$, the plane volumes $\omega_j$ and $\Omega_k$, hence the corners of $V_k$ (\claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported}), hence $V_k$ and recursively $W_k$ (\claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge}), are such products or diagonals of them. The ladder pairs: $v_j^* = \tfrac12(e_j + f_j)^* = \tfrac12(e_j - f_j) = w_j$. The maps: $\iota_k$ and $\theta_k$ send frame generators to frame generators or to $z \otimes 1$, so they intertwine the $*$'s; for $\varphi_k$ (\claimref{tower.commuting-copies}), equip $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\C)$ with the tensor $*$ (the ground $*$ on $A$, conjugate transpose on matrices) and check generators: $(x\,\Omega_k)^* = \Omega_k^*\, x^* = x^* \Omega_k$ since each $\omega_j^* = f_j^* e_j^* = (-f_j)(e_j) = e_j f_j = \omega_j$ and $\Omega_k$ commutes with ground generators, matching $(x \otimes 1)^* = x^* \otimes 1$; and the matrix units of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} satisfy $E_{12}^* = v^* = w = E_{21}$ and $E_{11}^* = (vw)^* = w^* v^* = vw = E_{11}$, matching the conjugate transpose, nested stage by stage.

\emph{The even case is a matrix *-algebra.} Let $m$ be even and represent on $(\C^2)^{\otimes m/2}$ by the tensor-Pauli assignment
\[
Y_{2l-1} := \sigma_z^{\otimes (l-1)} \otimes \sigma_x \otimes 1^{\otimes (m/2 - l)}, \qquad
Y_{2l} := \sigma_z^{\otimes (l-1)} \otimes \sigma_y \otimes 1^{\otimes (m/2 - l)} ,
\]
Hermitian unitaries that pairwise anticommute and square to one; the universal property gives a unital homomorphism $\pi : T_k^{\,\C} \to \Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$ with $\pi(y_i) = Y_i$, and $\pi$ is a *-homomorphism because $a \mapsto \pi(a^*)^*$ is again a homomorphism agreeing with $\pi$ on the generators. The $2^m$ blade images $Y_S := Y_{s_1} \cdots Y_{s_j}$ are, up to phase, distinct words in the Pauli basis, and distinct Pauli words are orthogonal for the trace form ($\operatorname{Tr}(Y_S^* Y_T) = 0$ for $S \neq T$), hence linearly independent: $\pi$ maps a basis to an independent set, so it is injective, and by the dimension count $2^m = (2^{m/2})^2$ it is a *-isomorphism onto the full matrix algebra, with $*$ the conjugate transpose.

\emph{Unique C*-norm, isometric inclusions.} In any C*-norm on $\Mat_N(\C)$, a self-adjoint $y$ has $\|y\| = \lim_j \|y^{2^j}\|^{1/2^j}$ (the C*-identity iterated) $=$ the spectral radius of $y$ (Gelfand's formula, valid in any finite-dimensional normed algebra), and then $\|x\|^2 = \|x^*x\| = \rho(x^* x)$ for every $x$: the norm is determined algebraically, hence unique. A unital *-monomorphism between floors pulls the target's C*-norm back to a C*-norm on the source, which by uniqueness is the source's own norm: the map is isometric. Finally, any C*-norm on $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ restricts on each floor to a C*-norm, hence to the unique one, so the norm on the union is determined.

tower.volume-elements-planes.formal: Let $\omega_j = e_j f_j$. Then $\omega_j^2 = 1$; $\omega_j$ anticommutes with $e_j$ and $f_j$; $\omega_j$ commutes with $e_i, f_i$ for $i \neq j$ and with every ground generator; and the $\omega_j$ commute pairwise. Hence $\Omega_k := \omega_1 \cdots \omega_k$ satisfies $\Omega_k^2 = 1$, commutes with all ground generators, and anticommutes with each $e_j, f_j$, $j \leq k$.
tower.volume-elements-planes.technical:
For each added plane with generators $e_j, f_j$, the plane volume element $\omega_j = e_j f_j$ satisfies $\omega_j^2 = 1$, anticommutes with $e_j$ and $f_j$, and commutes with the generators of every other plane and with every ground generator; the $\omega_j$ also commute pairwise. Each fact is a count of how many letters anticommute.

Consequently the product $\Omega_k = \omega_1 \cdots \omega_k$ satisfies $\Omega_k^2 = 1$, commutes with all ground generators, and anticommutes with each $e_j$ and $f_j$ for $j \leq k$.
tower.volume-elements-planes.lay: Each new plane added to the algebra has its own volume element, the product of its two generators. These elements square to one, flip the sign of their own plane's generators, and commute with everything else, including each other. Multiplying them all together gives a single element with the same behaviour towards all the added planes at once.
tower.volume-elements-planes.typing_note: Self-contained parity count with no store references, so no edges.

proofs.main: $\omega_j^2 = e_j f_j e_j f_j = -e_j^2 f_j^2 = -(1)(-1) = 1$, using $f_j e_j = -e_j f_j$ (\claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}). $\omega_j e_j = e_j f_j e_j = -e_j^2 f_j = -f_j$ while $e_j \omega_j = e_j e_j f_j = f_j$: they anticommute, and likewise for $f_j$. A ground generator or a generator of another plane anticommutes with both letters of $\omega_j$, hence commutes with their product. Pairwise commutation of the $\omega_j$ is the same parity count. The $\Omega_k$ statements follow: against $e_j$, exactly one factor ($\omega_j$) anticommutes.

tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity.formal: For any nondegenerate real quadratic space $(V, Q)$, the maximal number of pairwise-anticommuting fermionic mode pairs realisable by \emph{vectors} of $\Cl(V, Q)$ (families $(a_i, b_i)$ of vectors satisfying the displayed CAR of Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$ of $Q$. Along the tower the Witt index is $\min(p,q) + k$: each rung raises the algebra's mode capacity by exactly one, and by no more.
tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity.technical:
Let $(V, Q)$ be a nondegenerate real quadratic space of signature $(p,q)$, and call a family of vectors $(a_i, b_i)_{i \leq m}$ of $\Cl(V,Q)$ a mode family if it satisfies $a_i a_j + a_j a_i = 0$, $b_i b_j + b_j b_i = 0$ and $a_i b_j + b_j a_i = \delta_{ij}$. The largest possible $m$ is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$. For the upper bound, the relations force the $a_i$ to span a totally isotropic subspace, and pairing against the $b_j$ shows the $a_i$ are linearly independent; a totally isotropic subspace of a nondegenerate form of signature $(p,q)$ has dimension at most $\min(p,q)$. The bound is attained by the normalised null pairs of $\min(p,q)$ orthogonal hyperbolic planes split off by a Witt decomposition.

Along the tower, $T_k$ has signature $(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ and hence Witt index $\min(p,q) + k$, so each rung raises the number of vector-realised modes by exactly one and by no more.
tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity.lay: Inside a Clifford algebra one can ask how many independent fermionic modes can be built directly from vectors. The answer is a classical number attached to the geometry, the Witt index: the largest number of independent zero-length directions that are all orthogonal to one another. For a space with p positive and q negative directions it is the smaller of p and q. Each step up the tower raises this number by exactly one, so each step adds precisely one mode of capacity and no more.
tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity.typing_note: kept the CAR proposition as a premise because the mode families are defined by its displayed relations and the attainment step uses its null pairs; the upper bound itself is classical

proofs.main:
\emph{Upper bound.} Let $(a_i, b_i)_{i \leq m}$ be vectors satisfying the CAR. Reading the relations through the Clifford relation on vectors (\claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}): $\langle a_i, a_j \rangle = 0$ for all $i, j$ (including $i = j$), and $\langle a_i, b_j \rangle = \tfrac12 \delta_{ij}$. The span of the $a_i$ is therefore totally isotropic, and the $a_i$ are independent: a vanishing combination $\sum c_i a_i = 0$ pairs against $b_j$ to give $c_j/2 = 0$. So $m \leq$ the maximal totally isotropic dimension, which for a nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$ is $\min(p,q)$: diagonalise, $V = P \perp N$ with $P$ positive definite of dimension $p$ and $N$ negative definite of dimension $q$; a totally isotropic $U$ meets $P$ trivially (a nonzero $v \in U \cap P$ would have $Q(v) > 0$ and $Q(v) = 0$ at once), so the projection $U \to N$ along $P$ is injective and $\dim U \leq q$; symmetrically $\dim U \leq p$; and $\min(p,q)$ is attained by the null spans of $\min(p,q)$ hyperbolic pairs (the classical bound, cf.\ \cite[Ch.~I]{Lam2005}).

\emph{Attainment.} Split off $\min(p,q)$ orthogonal hyperbolic planes from $(V, Q)$ (Witt decomposition, \claimref{std-algebra.witt-decomposition}) and take their normalised null pairs, as in Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}. Along the tower, the form of signature $(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ has Witt index $\min(p,q) + k$, and each rung contributes its own plane to the attaining family.
